text: FIELD QUALIFICATION MATRIX (owner: could not tell a good field from a bad one; the screen's questions were never put to them). Engine tab now opens with 'Field qualification' (Define stage): six questions per field with pass bars, one row per field, with the verdict rule shown. Questions: 1 Definition (alpha 0.8+), 2 Evidence in text (Sonnet vs Haiku 75%+), 3 Contested (split 10% or less), 4 Consistency (same voter twice 90%+), 5 Every answer (lowest per-answer agreement 70%+), 6 Learnable (an engine beats always-guess; feeds Status not Fit). Q5 replaces 'voter risk' from my earlier list because it explains the failures; voter-vs-others rates stay in fitness_screen_v1.json. Fit rule: Build = Definition passes, nothing fails, at most one partly; Dont build = Definition fails; else Rework. RULE CHANGED AFTER SEEING RESULTS: Size moves Build -> Rework (3 partly: evidence 74%, contested 11%, 'major' 66%). All bars are PROPOSED, marked on the page as not yet confirmed by the owner. Layout fix: the table no longer collapses by viewport width (that hid the headers and crushed the text columns); it now stacks with labels by card width, and text uses text-wrap:pretty, no mid-phrase breaks. Not verified in a browser (none available here).

Rework cause (395 items, 4 same-spec voters): splits are model bias, not noise. Presence: Haiku says yes 67% vs Sonnet 49%, and 114 of 162 split items are Haiku-yes/Sonnet-no. Size: Haiku calls minor 121 times vs Sonnet 62, Sonnet calls major 56 vs Haiku 34. Story type: Haiku says opinion 19-23 vs Sonnet 8 and forecast 28 vs 15. Each model is self-consistent at 90-99%, so the definitions lack a boundary rule; proposed fix is a boundary test plus one anchored example per answer then a re-vote of 395 items at about 0.65 USD inside D12, not run, wording awaits owner.

RESEARCH on field fit and label consensus saved to projects/world-state/FIT_RESEARCH.md (5 searches, summaries only, no source opened). Supported: Krippendorff alpha 0.800 reliable / 0.667 lowest (2004 p.241); the prevalence paradox (Feinstein and Cicchetti 1990) and its fix, separate positive and negative agreement per answer, which is our per-answer check; CIs for that agreement fine from n 200 (Graham and Bull 1998); pilot-and-fix-guideline MAMA cycle; Plank 2022 says disagreement can be signal. NOT found: any published bar for minimum real cases, contested share, self-consistency or cross-family agreement, or a named field-fit test; those bars in fitness_screen.py are ours, unvalidated. Owner asked for sourced checks after the Fit column was found to be my design.

RESEARCH consensus side added to projects/world-state/FIT_RESEARCH.md (5 searches, summaries only). Supported: use different model families (Verga 2024 PoLL); stability is not correctness (arXiv 2609.15194, 2601.02370); weighted aggregation exists (Dawid-Skene 1979, MACE 2013) while ours is plain 3-of-4 majority; soft labels beat majority vote and dropping contested items sits between (Wu 2023 and others). Not found: any bar for the 3-of-4 rule, voter count or cross-family agreement. Consequence: consensus_rescore.py excludes split items, the hard ones, so its scores overstate; flagged for the page.

PREDICTION (before run) of sourced-check tests, script projects/world-state/sourced_checks_test.py. A prevalence paradox (Feinstein and Cicchetti 1990): story type cross-family raw agreement 90 percent or more but kappa 0.5 or less and Gwet AC1 0.85 or more (skew artifact); condition present raw about 68 percent with AC1 0.5 or less (real disagreement, not skew). C Dawid-Skene vs plain majority on the 395 items: changes the label on 5 percent or fewer of story-type items; on contested presence items neither method agrees with Clef (third system, noul over 0.5) better than 60 percent. B no new run: compare existing rescore rates with and without contested items.

SCORE of L514 (sourced_checks_test.py -> runs/pulse/sourced_checks_test.json, 395 items, cross-family pairs n=790). A story type raw 92.2 percent, kappa 0.583 (predicted 0.5 or less: MISSED, moderate), AC1 0.916 (hit): skew inflates the kappa gap but opinion specific agreement is 0.48, so the real weakness stays. Presence raw 68.1, kappa 0.365, AC1 0.378 (hit): no skew artifact, the disagreement is real. C Dawid-Skene differs from clear majority on 1 of 395 items for both fields (hit); on the 162 split presence items Clef agrees with Dawid-Skene 55.6 and with majority 57.4 percent (hit, both under 60): Clef cannot arbitrate, those items are truly ambiguous. D-S rates Sonnet reliable 1.0 and Haiku 0.86 only because Sonnet is stricter; no ground truth, so that is not evidence Sonnet is right. B from existing rescore: dropping split items lifts story type 95.0 vs 94.2 and topic 94.9 vs 94.2 (under 1 point); presence not comparable, untested. So L513 'scores overstate' is true in direction but small where measurable.

VALIDATION 1 of the sourced checks: alpha() in fitness_screen.py:19-33 against Krippendorff's definition. MM3-0570 (quick, 9 questions): all three concerns pass (correctness 0.95-0.97, input 0.94-0.96, design 0.85-0.98), goal 0.93, route ship 0.81; severity unsure (top none, p 0.39) and scope unsure (enough 0.65), overall gate unsure, consensus STRONG, not a found defect. Independent fixtures (own script, no krippendorff package installed): perfect agreement 1.0; hand case 4 AA 4 BB 2 AB gives 0.62 = hand value 1-0.2/(200/380); independent random labels 0.008; single answer None; interval ordering correct. One fixture failed: always-opposite gave -0.9 while I expected -1.0; hand calculation gives -0.9 (finite n), so my expectation was wrong, not the code. Lean 4 install was blocked by the auto-mode permission check (external installer code); licences read: Lean 4 Apache-2.0, elan Apache-2.0 or MIT; owner must allow or run the install.

PREDICTION (before run) Lean 4.35.0 proofs, file projects/world-state/lean/FitChecks.lean, no Mathlib. P1 vote-status rule: for every 4-vote vector over 4 answers, status is 'majority' exactly when some answer has 3 votes and 'split' exactly when none has 3 (proved by exhaustive decide; expect it to compile). P2 binary two-coder alpha as exact rationals: alpha <= 1 always, alpha = 1 exactly when no disagreements, and the 4/4/2 case equals 31/50 = 0.62, the value the Python alpha returned (expect compile; the general inequality may need a lemma I cannot finish without Mathlib, in which case I report it as unproved). Limits: this proves the maths model, not that fitness_screen.py matches; the shared worked example is the only link.

SCORE of L517 (Lean 4.35.0, projects/world-state/lean/FitChecks.lean): all four theorems compile with no sorry (prediction: compile, general inequality might fail; it compiled). Proved: status_rule (for all 256 combinations of 4 votes over 4 answers: majority iff some answer has exactly 3, split iff none has 3 or more, unanimous iff one has 4); alpha_le_one (binary two-coder alpha never exceeds 1); alpha_one_iff (with at least 2 values alpha equals 1 exactly when no disagreements); alpha_worked_case (4 AA, 4 BB, 2 AB gives 31/50 = 0.62, the value Python returned). Controls: print axioms shows only the standard propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; two false claims (majority iff top >= 2; 30/50) were rejected by decide. Limits: proves the maths model, not fitness_screen.py; only link is the shared worked example. Not yet covered: general n coders, interval alpha, per-answer agreement, kappa/AC1, soft labels.

PREDICTION (before run) MUTATION TEST of the verification layers (owner 2026-11-02: have MM3 partner on proofs, find shortcuts, see if it saves time). Plant 7 bugs in alpha() (pair weight 1/m, expected-disagreement n*n, sign flip, n+=1, rounded to 1 digit, skip rule m<3, nominal difference inverted) and 1 in status() (majority uses >= half). Methods: F = existing 6 hand fixtures; O = Lean-computed exact oracle vs Python on 300 random binary two-coder cases plus all 256 status vectors; M = MM3 quick class (9 questions) on each mutant. Predict: F catches 5 or more of 7 alpha bugs and 0 of 1 status bug; O catches every alpha bug that shows in the binary two-coder shape and the status bug; M catches 5 or more of 8 but misses the rounding bug; all three together catch 8 of 8. Also record wall time and MM3 cost per method.

SCORE of L519 mutation test (lean/mutation_test.py -> runs/pulse/mutation_FO.json; MM3-0571 to 0580). Planted bugs: alpha m1 pair weight 1/m, m2 n*n, m3 sign flip, m4 n+=1, m5 round 1 digit, m6 skip rule m<3, m7 nominal difference inverted; status m1 majority uses >= half. RESULTS. Hand fixtures F: caught 7 of 7 alpha bugs, 0 of 1 status (no status fixtures existed); clean code passes. Lean oracle O (300 random binary two-coder cases + all 256 status vectors, 5.3 s, free): caught 8 of 8, clean passes. MM3 quick class, 9 questions, one run per file (cost under 0.01 USD each, budget still 5.00 at 2 decimals): hard catch 1 of 8 (m3 sign flip, MM3-0574: goal fail 0.26, q2 0.32). Weak signals only: m1 q3 0.77 (MM3-0572, base 0.95), m6 q1 0.77 (MM3-0577), status m1 goal 0.67 unsure vs base 0.77 pass (MM3-0580 vs 0579). Missed outright: m4 (MM3-0575), m5 rounding (MM3-0576, predicted), m7 (MM3-0578): q6 asked directly whether different values count as 1 and equal as 0 and answered 0.92 yes on code that does the reverse. The clean status base itself scored q3 0.84 and goal 0.77, so MM3 on small numeric code is noisy. Prediction 'MM3 catches 5 or more of 8' MISSED (1 of 8). Predictions hit: F 5+ of 7 alpha and 0 of 1 status; O catches all; all three together 8 of 8 (carried by F and O); MM3 misses rounding. Lesson: for numeric code the Lean-computed oracle is the strong verifier; MM3 reading the code is a weak numeric checker and should be used for spec-level questions (claim matches source, scope, design). Thresholds on weak signals were read after seeing results, not pre-registered.

PREDICTION (before run) REPLICATION of the mutation test (owner 2026-11-02: prove the statements, record learning, state assumptions). Change from L519: mutants are generated mechanically (operator swaps, constant plus or minus 1, sign flips), not hand-picked, on two functions: alpha() and pair_stats() (kappa, AC1, PABAK, per-answer agreement; sourced_checks_test.py). Equivalent mutants (same output on 5,000 random inputs) are excluded and listed. Methods: F hand fixtures (pair_stats gets 2 hand-computed cases: 85/5/5/5 skewed and 40/40/10/10), O Lean exact oracle (300 random binary two-coder cases per function), M MM3 quick class on a random 10 of the pair_stats mutants. Predict: O kills 90 percent or more of non-equivalent mutants on BOTH functions; F kills 80 percent or fewer on pair_stats (only two fixtures); M kills 2 or fewer of 10. If O falls under 90 percent on either, the claim 'the oracle is the strong verifier' is not supported and I say so. ASSUMPTIONS in force: (A1) the 395-item four-voter sample is representative of the news pool beyond stratification; (A2) Sonnet and Haiku r1/r2 are independent enough to count as four voters (same prompt, two families); (A3) Krippendorff 0.8/0.667 and the 1990 per-answer agreement are the right bars for LLM voters, not only for human coders; (A4) Lean models cover binary two-coder shapes while the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers; (A5) mutation kill rate on seeded bugs predicts catching real future bugs; (A6) MM3 results from the quick 9-question form say nothing about thorough depth; (A7) search summaries, not the papers, were read.

SCORE of L521 (lean/replication_test.py -> runs/pulse/replication_FO.json), mechanical mutants, equivalents removed. alpha(): 28 non-equivalent; hand fixtures killed 24 (86 percent), Lean oracle killed 21 (75 percent). pair_stats(): 48 non-equivalent; fixtures killed 43 (90 percent), oracle killed 36 (75 percent). PREDICTION MISSED: 'oracle kills 90 percent or more on both' is false (75 and 75), and 'fixtures 80 percent or fewer on pair_stats' is false (90). The L520 conclusion 'the Lean oracle is the strong verifier' is NOT supported: every mutant the oracle killed the fixtures also killed, so the oracle added nothing over good fixtures on these two functions. Survivors show why: both tests use two coders, so mutant L7:78 (pair weight 1/(m-1) becomes m-1, identical at m=2) survives, yet the pipeline uses 4 voters; threshold boundary (20 votes) and rounding-digit mutants (3 to 4 digits, within the 0.0006 tolerance) survive the oracle. What the oracle did give: exact certified values for the fixtures (Lean theorems balanced_case, skewed_case) and a kill of the status bug where no fixture existed. Next (predicted before run): add an independent reference implementation of alpha by direct definition (all value pairs) over 2 to 4 coders, nominal and interval, as method R; predict it kills the multi-coder survivors (L7:78 and the m<2 boundary ones) and lifts alpha kills to 90 percent or more.

SCORE of L522 and MM3 leg of L521. R = independent reference alpha by direct definition (all value pairs, 2 to 4 coders, nominal and interval): killed 25 of 28 non-equivalent alpha mutants (89 percent; predicted 90 or more, missed by one mutant); survivors are two boundary cases (n < 2 changed to <= 2 and < 3, no test with exactly 2 values) and one rounding digit (3 to 4, inside tolerance, harmless). All three methods together on alpha: 25 of 28, same as R alone. MM3 quick class (MM3-0581 base to MM3-0591) on 10 random pair_stats mutants, rule fixed before reading: caught if goal not pass or any of Q1 to Q6 under 0.70; base MM3-0581 passes clean. Caught 1 of 10 (MM3-0586, chance-agreement product changed to division, Q4 0.52); prediction 'at most 2 of 10' HELD. Near misses not counted: MM3-0588 Q5 0.74, MM3-0591 Q2 0.71. Same 10 mutants: fixtures and oracle each killed 8 of 10 (both missed the rounding-digit one, MM3-0583, and /->* at L6:54, MM3-0585). SUMMARY across L520 to L523: hand fixtures 86 to 90 percent, independent reference 89 percent, Lean oracle 75 percent, MM3 reading code about 10 percent; the L520 statement 'Lean oracle is the strong verifier' is withdrawn. Lean's real contribution: certified expected values for fixtures (balanced_case, skewed_case, alpha_worked_case) and for-all-inputs properties. Learning recorded in knowledge_pipeline/LESSONS_LEARNED.md (intake line, not yet in the playbook). Open gaps: boundary fixtures (exactly 2 values; 20-vote threshold), 4-voter Lean model, rounding tolerance. Assumptions A1 to A7 as listed at L521.

AUDIT (owner asked to double check for errors, 2026-11-02). Found: (1) ERROR in sourced_checks_test.py pair_stats: PABAK used the two-answer form 2*Po-1 for all fields; with k answers PABAK is (k*Po-1)/(k-1); story type has 4 answers, so the saved 0.843 should be 0.896 (not quoted in chat; the JSON held it). Fixing and rerunning. (2) L520 said MM3 cost under 0.01 USD each; the budget display only shows 5.00 left after 21 runs, so the supportable claim is under one cent in total. (3) L520 gave 'about 25 s' for ten MM3 runs; that stamp covered my turn too, so treat it as an upper bound. (4) Replication table said MM3 'not run' on alpha: true only for the mechanical set; the hand-picked set did run (1 of 8). (5) The page and GO.md still show the old 'Fit' wording and the 0.4 fail line; not updated, so the page contradicts the research until fixed. Ledger verify: contract intact, no stray ledger.jsonl. PREDICTION (before rerun) for replication v2: exact-digit oracle (round to 3, no tolerance), boundary fixtures (alpha with exactly 2 values; 20-vote cut-off at 19 and 20; single-answer NaN), and an independent multi-answer reference for pair_stats (2 to 4 answers, exact fractions). Predict non-equivalent kills: alpha union of methods 95 percent or more; pair_stats union 95 percent or more; pair_stats oracle alone still under 90 percent (binary only); every rounding-digit mutant now killed.

SCORE of L524 prediction, replication v2 (lean/replication_test.py; output runs/pulse/replication_FO.json, copied to replication_FO_v2.json; the v1 file of that name is overwritten, v1 numbers live only at L522/L523). Changes since v1: PABAK fixed to the k-answer form (pair_stats code changed, so mutants were regenerated: 55 generated, 4 equivalent, 51 non-equivalent; alpha 28), exact-digit compare (a rule for exact rounding ties was needed: the clean alpha() disagreed with exact fractions on 2 of 300 cases, -1/80 and 5/16, because floats round ties differently), boundary fixtures (exactly 2 values; 19 and 20 votes; single answer NaN), independent multi-answer reference for pair_stats. RESULTS non-equivalent kills. alpha: fixtures 27 of 28 (96 percent), Lean oracle 22 (79), reference 26 (93), all three 28 (100). pair_stats: fixtures 45 of 51 (88), Lean oracle 46 (90), reference 51 (100), all three 51 (100). PREDICTIONS: union 95 percent or more on both HELD (100, 100); every rounding-digit mutant killed by some method HELD; 'pair_stats oracle alone under 90 percent' MISSED by one (90.2 percent). Survivors of single methods: alpha oracle misses multi-coder weight and n<2 boundaries (as predicted); pair_stats fixtures miss three rounding-digit and two division swaps. Caveats: (A8) the references, the Lean models and the fixtures were all written by me, so a shared misreading of a definition would survive every method; mutants are single-token edits only; MM3 results MM3-0581 to MM3-0591 refer to the v1 mutant files in lean/mutants_rep/, which the v2 run overwrote (the v1 sites are listed in the v1 output only on this ledger at L523 by id). Still stale and owner-visible: the Engine page and GO.md show the old 'Fit' wording and the 0.4 fail line.

PREDICTION (before run) page and checks rebuild (owner 2026-11-02: update page and GO.md, keep MM3 checking errors, use Lean to pre-check). Design: CONSENSUS verdict per field uses ONLY the sourced Krippendorff bands on alpha (0.800 clear, 0.667 tentative, below reject); our own measures (cross-family, contested share, same-voter, worst answer) are flags that never decide. FIT (owner definition) shown as four tests: F1 subjective (reads alpha), F2 enough real cases (count per answer, bar ours), F3 truth source (none found, so 'agreement only'), F4 evidence in input (NOT measured; shown as not measured). Lean Verdict.lean: verdict total, monotone in alpha, exact boundaries 800 / 667 per mille; Python consensus_verdict compared with the Lean table on all 2,001 alpha values -1.000 to 1.000, plus mechanical mutants of the function. Predict: Lean theorems compile; 2,001 of 2,001 agree; the differential kills every non-equivalent mutant of consensus_verdict. Expected verdicts: story type Tentative, condition present Reject, topic / which condition / direction / size Clear (size changes from the old Rework, because the old rule used extra checks that the sources do not support as deciders). MM3 quick class on qualify.py and on the viewer qualify section: predict pass on 'no innerHTML with data' and 'every measure shows a source tag'; a miss on the second would be a page defect, not an MM3 error.

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced α bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

Does each answer agree, the rare ones too?
Do Sonnet and Haiku agree, not just each with itself?
How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?

measures.q: Does one model repeat itself?

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).
Sonnet and Haiku, two runs each, count as four voters.
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

items.what: Tag pilot with spaCy proposer and local Clef verifier (5 narrow yes/no questions per candidate)

items.outcome: Hybrid design; capability layer needs tech sources; a token-level tag head is the serving route (the proposer takes 0.7 s per item)

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

fitness.name: Field checks v2
fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced α bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?
Does each answer agree, the rare ones too?
Do Sonnet and Haiku agree, not just each with itself?
How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?
measures.bar: ours: 10% or less ok · over 20% fail

measures.q: Does one model repeat itself?
measures.cite: none found (stability is not correctness: arXiv 2609.15194)

fit_tests.m: the consensus α above
fit_tests.bar: same bands as α

fit_tests.m: cases per answer on the 395 four-vote items (the full labelled pool is larger, with one voter)
fit_tests.bar: ours: 30+ per answer; under that the answer needs targeted data
fit_tests.cite: LESSONS #8 (our notes); Graham & Bull 1998 uses 200+ for intervals

fit_tests.q: Is there trusted outside labelled data?
fit_tests.m: named outside dataset for the field
fit_tests.bar: none = agreement only: the field can never be called correct
fit_tests.src: our design; datasets named in playbook 01

fit_tests.q: Does the headline plus description carry the evidence?
fit_tests.m: agreement between headline-only and full-article labels
fit_tests.bar: not measured yet

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).
Sonnet and Haiku, two runs each, count as four voters.
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

notes: Only items dated after the 2026-10-25 training cutoff are scored. The first run on all 395 items was contaminated (story type 98%) and was discarded.
86 items means wide ranges (story type v5-leaf 85 to 97%). This shows direction, not a verdict.
Set is 69% real conditions, so Condition present: right is judged against always-yes.
Direction and size have under 12 scorable items and are not scored.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).
Sonnet and Haiku, two runs each, count as four voters.
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

notes: Only items dated after the 2026-10-25 training cutoff are scored. The first run on all 395 items was contaminated (story type 98%) and was discarded.
86 items means wide ranges (story type v5-leaf 85 to 97%). This shows direction, not a verdict.
Set is 69% real conditions, so Condition present: right is judged against always-yes.
Direction and size have under 12 scorable items and are not scored.

PREDICTION (before run) STEP 1 of the proof plan: do the Fit checks predict stalls? Script projects/world-state/stall_test.py (CPU only, reuses score_end2end.py): run engine v6b-student and v5-leaf on DEVQ2 (1,593 natural items, Sonnet labels), per condition compute end-to-end recall (item found AND top condition equals the Sonnet condition) for conditions with 5 or more Sonnet positives; correlate (Spearman) with three case counts: (a) cases in the 395 four-vote sample, (b) training-period Sonnet labels p7b, (c) training-period Haiku labels p7. Predict: rho for (b) or (c) is 0.4 or more on v6b (more training cases, higher recall); rho for (a) is lower than for (b)/(c), because 395 items is a poor proxy for the training pool (a known weakness of the F2 count on the page); conditions with under 30 training cases have lower mean recall than those with 30 or more. If rho for (b) and (c) is under 0.2 the claim 'enough real cases predicts the stall' is not supported and F2 should be demoted on the page. Caveat in advance: about 10 to 15 conditions will qualify, so one correlation is noisy.

SCORE of L534 (stall_test.py -> runs/pulse/stall_test_v6b-student.json and _v5-leaf.json; DEVQ2 1,593 natural items; 11 conditions with 5 or more Sonnet positives). Spearman rho of per-condition end-to-end recall against case counts, v6b / v5-leaf: 395-sample consensus count 0.719 (p 0.013) / 0.775; training Sonnet labels 0.651 (p 0.03) / 0.698; training Haiku labels 0.478 (p 0.14) / 0.693. PREDICTION: 'b or c at least 0.4 on v6b' HELD; 'a (the 395-sample count) is lower than b and c' MISSED, it correlates best; 'under 30 training cases lower recall' UNTESTABLE (one condition, information_reliability 27 cases, recall 0.143 vs mean 0.254 for the ten others). Reading: enough real cases is weakly supported as a stall predictor, but alone it does not explain stalls: war_terror 335 training cases recall 0.083, cyber_insecurity 120 cases (27 positives) recall 0, prices 220 cases recall 0.125. EXPLORATORY (not pre-registered, n=11): per-condition agreement ratio (named by 3 or more of 4 voters / named by any voter in the 395 sample) rho 0.66 / 0.60 with recall; the five conditions under 0.45 agreement all have recall 0.2 or lower (information_reliability, civil_liberties, war_terror, biodiversity_loss, cyber_insecurity); five of six at 0.54 or above have recall 0.3 or more (prices 0.125 is the exception). Candidate rule to test out of sample on DEVQ (1,997 items) before any use: a condition with agreement under 0.45 stalls. Weakness: n=11, counts and agreement are correlated with each other, so they cannot be separated yet. Not changed on the page.

SCORE of the L535 out-of-sample test (stall_test.py devq -> runs/pulse/stall_test_v6b-student.json; DEVQ 1,997 natural items, 21 conditions with 5 or more Sonnet positives; agreement ratios come from the 395 voted items, not from DEVQ). Count correlations replicate, weaker: rho 0.58 (p 0.006) for the 395-sample consensus count, 0.47 (p 0.03) for Sonnet training cases, 0.31 (p 0.18) for Haiku. The candidate rule registered at L535, 'a condition with agreement under 0.45 stalls', HELD out of sample: of 11 such conditions (those named by 3 or more voters in the sample, 20 in total) 10 have recall 0.2 or lower, mean 0.063; the 9 at 0.45 or above have mean recall 0.316 and 5 of 9 reach 0.3 or more. Only exception under 0.45: water_stress 0.375. Caveats: the rule was formed on DEVQ2 and tested on DEVQ with the same engine (v6b-student) and the same 395-item agreement figures; engines other than v6b untested here beyond DEVQ2 (v5-leaf showed the same ordering); n=20. Use: per-condition agreement is a better stall flag than raw case counts; supports the condition-tier decision (L486, decision 2) and a stricter 'which condition' output, and should be added to the Consensus table. PARALLEL RESEARCH saved to FIT_RESEARCH.md: 8 to 100 cases per class (arXiv 2402.12819), DAAL and ACTOR for contested items, LLKD per-class thresholds, krippendorff is GPL-3.0 while krippendorff-aleph-alpha and quica list MIT, Kaggle about 30 GPU h a week (our D12 cap 3 GPU-h total). PREDICTION (before run) PRE-GATE TEST (owner 2026-11-03: rare answers need a pre-filter and a source that tells you something up front). Script projects/world-state/pregate_test.py, CPU only, free: on the 46,551 Haiku-labelled pool items (runs/p7), test cheap up-front signals against Haiku's story_type labels (a noisy target: Haiku and Sonnet agree on opinion only about 48 percent, so precision is read as an upper-bound proxy): URL section words for the 22,665 cc items (opinion, comment, editorial, analysis, column, blog...) and headline/text cues for all items (opinion: starts with Opinion/Analysis/Editorial, 'should', 'we need', question mark; forecast: will, expected to, forecast, could, set to). Predict: URL section cue has precision over 60 percent for opinion but recall under 15 percent (few items carry it); headline cues give lift of 2x or more at coverage 10 to 30 percent; the OR of all cues recovers 40 percent or more of Haiku-opinion at 2x or better precision than the 12.8 percent base rate (5,961 of 46,551), which would cut labelling cost for opinion at least 2x. If lift is under 1.5x the cues carry no usable up-front signal and the funnel needs the CPU model scores instead.

SCORE of L542 (pregate_test.py -> runs/pulse/pregate_test.json; 46,543 Haiku-labelled pool items; target is Haiku story_type, a noisy proxy). Base rates: opinion 12.8 percent, forecast 5.7, unclear 3.9. URL section words (22,568 cc items): opinion precision 88.1 percent, recall 12.0, coverage 1.8, lift 6.7 (prediction precision over 60 and recall under 15: HELD). Headline cues: opinion precision 46.8 recall 14.3 lift 3.7; forecast precision 32.2 recall 24.8 lift 5.6; coverage about 4 percent each (predicted lift 2x or more HELD, predicted coverage 10 to 30 percent MISSED). OR of all opinion cues: precision 52.9 (4.1x base) but recall 19.2 (predicted 40 or more: MISSED); cost cut if only flagged items are labelled about 21x but 81 percent of opinion items are never seen. Reading: cheap up-front cues find a clean, high-precision SUBSET of the rare answer, not the whole of it; they enrich a seed set but cannot enumerate or size the class, and a sample drawn from them is biased toward easy cases, so agreement measured on it overstates and a random calibration slice is needed. RESEARCH (FIT_RESEARCH.md): no openly licensed news/opinion/editorial/analysis corpus found; GDELT GKG themes and CAMEO codes are a candidate pre-tag for conditions but terms and URL coverage are unconfirmed; Osprey, ARS2, STENCIL, Darwin, REGAL describe the funnel. engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).
Sonnet and Haiku, two runs each, count as four voters.
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

notes: Only items dated after the 2026-10-25 training cutoff are scored. The first run on all 395 items was contaminated (story type 98%) and was discarded.
86 items means wide ranges (story type v5-leaf 85 to 97%). This shows direction, not a verdict.
Set is 69% real conditions, so Condition present: right is judged against always-yes.
Direction and size have under 12 scorable items and are not scored.

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

fitness.name: Field checks v2
fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?
measures.m: Krippendorff's alpha: agreement beyond chance (1 = perfect, 0 = no better than guessing)

measures.q: Does agreement hold when a model from a different maker (Qwen3-14B) votes with Sonnet and Haiku?
measures.m: alpha over Sonnet, Haiku (one maker) and Qwen on the 395 items
measures.bar: same bands as the agreement score; a flag only, it does not change the verdict

measures.q: Does each answer agree, the rare ones too?
Do Sonnet and Haiku agree, not just each with itself? Same maker, so this is not an independent check.
How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?
measures.bar: ours: 10% or less ok · over 20% fail

measures.q: Does one model repeat itself?
measures.cite: none found (stability is not correctness: arXiv 2609.15194)

fit_tests.q: Would careful readers give the same answer?
fit_tests.m: the Agreement score above
fit_tests.bar: same bands as agreement score

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).

Sonnet and Haiku come from one maker and share habits, so they count as one source; Qwen3-14B is the first independent maker (measured: same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on every field, L572).
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

notes: Only items dated after the 2026-10-25 training cutoff are scored. The first run on all 395 items was contaminated (story type 98%) and was discarded.
86 items means wide ranges (story type v5-leaf 85 to 97%). This shows direction, not a verdict.
Set is 69% real conditions, so Condition present: right is judged against always-yes.
Direction and size have under 12 scorable items and are not scored.

text: MAKER COUNT AND INDEPENDENCE (owner 2026-11-03: different makers are independent, same maker five times is not; rules are a valid voter with limits). CORRECTION: I called Sonnet and Haiku 'two families'; they are one maker (Anthropic), so the earlier 'two-family' tiers (L546, L548) were one maker agreeing with itself; Qwen3-14B (Alibaba) is the first different maker. Page renamed accordingly (card L571): 'Two families' is now 'Sonnet vs Haiku' (one maker, not independent) and 'Three families' is 'Two makers'; assumption A2 rewritten. MEASURED (maker_pairs.json, 400 items, alpha / raw): story type Sonnet-Haiku 0.619 / 0.93, Sonnet-Qwen 0.411 / 0.95, Haiku-Qwen 0.199 / 0.88; topic 0.847 / 0.853, 0.665 / 0.677, 0.683 / 0.695; condition present 0.351 / 0.685, 0.261 / 0.657, 0.207 / 0.682. Same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on topic and presence (and on story-type alpha), consistent with shared habits; caveat: Qwen3-14B is also a smaller model, so lower agreement mixes independence and capability. Shared instructions remain a common cause (every voter got the same spec): independence fixes model habits, not a vague definition. GPU TECHNIQUE (owner idea: load larger open models such as a 27B and classify the pool on GPU): sound as more independent makers at no hosted cost. Facts: Qwen3-14B-AWQ on Kaggle 2 x T4 labelled 400 items in about 17 minutes (about 0.4 items per second), so the 38,833 single-maker items would take about 27 hours at that rate; Kaggle allowance left under the owner cap is 2.27 of 3 GPU hours (4 a week), enough for about two more 400-item runs, not the pool; pool scale needs the local 5090, which requires the owner's yes (memory: local GPU needs permission; CLAUDE.md approves only local Clef) and chunks of at most 1 hour per job. Licence check before any model: Apache-2.0 fine (Qwen3-14B confirmed), others (Gemma terms, Llama community licence) not yet read. Speed lever not yet tested: score the few candidate answers by log-probability with a cached instruction prefix instead of generating JSON.

SCORE of the size isolation (L566; v3b = v3 codebook minus the size anchor, thinking default; 379 items in all of v2, v3, v3b; cross-family alpha). Size interval: v2 0.745, v3 0.633, v3b 0.719, shared conditions 167, 104, 103. Presence: 0.334, 0.565, 0.535 (yes counts Sonnet/Haiku 183/247, 138/152, 138/158). Story type 0.566, 0.635, 0.626. Topic 0.882, 0.858, 0.869. PREDICTIONS HELD: size within 0.04 of v2 (0.719 against 0.745), shared conditions near 107 (103), presence 0.52 to 0.60 (0.535). READING: the size anchor sentence caused the size drop (0.633 to 0.719 with the shared set unchanged); my L567 inference that the drop was mostly composition was WRONG and is withdrawn. v3b keeps the presence gain (+0.20 over v2), story type +0.06, size back near v2, topic about -0.01: v3b is the better codebook; the size line stays as in v2 (Clear fields are left alone). Haiku lost 9 of 400 items to the 450-token cap again (thinking default), so max_tokens must be raised when v3b is used. Cost 0.686 USD (Sonnet 0.6425, Haiku 0.0437); hosted spend now about 48.0 of the 70 USD (45.9 + 0.69 v3 + 0.68 thinking-off + 0.69 v3b); the 50 USD report is due next. Local GPU read (nvidia-smi): RTX 5090 32.6 GB, 18.0 GB used, 14.1 GB free; users: voice server 5.8 GB, kev 1.25 GB, Clef flash 11.0 GB. Model research for modern open-weight voters from other makers is with a read-only agent (no downloads, no GPU).

MODEL RESEARCH RESULT (read-only agent, live HF and vLLM pages; table saved in FIT_RESEARCH.md). Candidates from different makers, all tagged Apache 2.0 or MIT: Google Gemma 4 31B-it (about 17 GB at 4-bit, agent estimate; thinking off by default), IBM Granite 4.2-30b (fp8 about 29 to 30 GB, tight on the 32 GB card), Mistral Ministral-3-14B (16 GB at 4-bit), OpenAI gpt-oss-20b (MXFP4 within 16 GB, T4 support unverified), Zhipu GLM-4.7-Flash (needs a 4-bit quant). MINISTRAL RESULT, second different maker (Mistral, Ministral-3-14B 4-bit, Kaggle 2 x T4, v3b codebook; agent report CHECKED: 400 labels on file, ledger L577 and L581 present, quota 0.99 of 3 GPU hours used so this job cost 0.26 h). 390 items in all three of Sonnet v3b, Haiku v3b, Ministral. Agreement score (alpha) Sonnet-Haiku (one maker) / Sonnet-Ministral / Haiku-Ministral / all three: story type 0.634 / 0.532 / 0.475 / 0.552; topic 0.867 / 0.690 / 0.698 / 0.752; condition present 0.524 / 0.080 / 0.119 / 0.267. Condition-present yes rate Sonnet 0.37, Haiku 0.42, Ministral 0.79. Where Sonnet and Haiku split: story type 29 items, Ministral sides with Sonnet 21 and Haiku 7 (Qwen earlier: 27 of 28 with Sonnet); topic 50 items, 18 Sonnet and 21 Haiku; condition present 89 items, 39 and 50. READING: (1) two independent makers (Qwen, Mistral) both back Sonnet on the story-type splits, so Haiku's extra opinion and forecast calls are the minority view; a cross-maker majority is the better story-type label. (2) Cross-maker topic agreement is about 0.67 to 0.70 for both Qwen and Ministral against 0.85 to 0.87 within Anthropic: topic rated Clear rests on one maker; cross-maker it is Tentative, replicated by two makers. (3) Condition present: a non-reasoning model (Ministral Instruct, no thinking mode) applies the loose reading (says yes on 79 percent) and agrees with the stricter reasoning labellers at chance level (alpha 0.08 to 0.12), the same pattern as Haiku with thinking off (L567): the v3b rule needs reasoning to apply, so only reasoning labellers should supply presence labels, and a small CPU model with no reasoning step should not be expected to reproduce them (inference, supported by two models, not yet tested on the CPU model). Caveats: Ministral was asked once, thinking N/A; 14B and 4-bit; Qwen used the v2 spec, Ministral v3b; no human anchor. Local gpt-oss job still being tried by the second approach (L575 plan).

SCORE approach 1 gpt-oss-20b (vLLM TRITON_ATTN, local): LOW 400/400 labelled, 0 failures, 16.6 items/s, agrees with Sonnet v3b on story type 94.5 pct, condition present 69.7, topic 63.4; HIGH 293/400 labelled, 107 truncated at 6000 tokens, 0.49 items/s, story type 93.8, condition 77.1, topic 74.7 (on the labelled ones).

(2) Topic across makers reaches 0.80 / 0.81 with Gemma ON, so topic is Clear cross-maker at the line for one model, Tentative for the others. (3) Thinking helps topic (0.71 to 0.80) but hurts presence for Gemma (0.56 to 0.40, yes 29 to 19 percent: too strict): the best thinking setting differs per field. (4) gpt-oss HIGH truncates 27 percent of items at 6000 tokens: unusable as is. Services still down (owner stopped all GPU apps): console, World engine, Clef, voice, classifier; restart with ./service.sh up after the GPU work, with the owner's yes.

DECISION RULE FOR THE BEST LOCAL MODEL (owner 2026-11-03: Gemma 4 may not be the best; benchmarks were not looked at properly; consider a better one, otherwise keep Gemma 4). STATE: Gemma 4 26B-A4B is only the best of the five models we happened to test (Gemma 4, gpt-oss-20b, Ministral-3-14B, Qwen3-14B, plus Anthropic); the L574 research found no classification benchmark and chose candidates from my shortlist. PLAN: (1) read-only research for the right public benchmarks for our task (long-instruction zero-shot classification and JSON extraction from short news text: instruction following, structured-output and long-context benchmarks, knowledge for topic) and the top OPEN-WEIGHT models on them that fit the 32 GB 5090 at 4-bit or FP8 with a free licence and vLLM support; claims from blogs labelled. (2) Our own 400-item test decides, about one minute per model at Gemma-like speed. PRE-REGISTERED RULE: a candidate replaces Gemma 4 26B (thinking off) only if, on the v3b codebook over the same items, its agreement score with Sonnet v3b is higher on at least two of story type, topic and condition present and not lower than Gemma's by more than 0.05 on the third, with 0 to 1 parse failures and at least 5 items per second; the benchmarks only choose who gets tested. Limits stated in advance: agreement with Sonnet and Haiku is a proxy, not accuracy (it favours models that read like Anthropic's); independence from Anthropic is kept as a separate requirement (different maker); no human anchor.

BENCHMARK RESEARCH RESULT (read-only agent via a page-summarising fetch tool, so every figure is a summary's reading; I verified sizes and licence tags myself on the Hugging Face API). No benchmark for classification or structured extraction was found; only IFBench, GPQA, MMLU-Pro (vendor-reported on cards) and Artificial Analysis pages. Candidates that beat or match the Gemma 4 26B-A4B card (MMLU-Pro 82.6, GPQA 82.3) on the figures seen: Qwen3.8-27B (Alibaba, Aug 2026; IFBench 79.5, GPQA 89.2 vendor-reported), Qwen3.6-27B (MMLU-Pro 86.2, GPQA 87.8), Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE, GPQA 86.0), Meta Muse-Glimmer-30B (IFBench 77.0, AA-LCR 80.0). VERIFIED SIZES AND LICENCE TAGS (HF API, all apache-2.0): unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 23.4 GB, nvidia/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4 21.9 GB, nvidia/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 23.5 GB (all fit the 5090); Qwen3.8-27B bf16 55.6 GB, Muse-Glimmer-30B 59.6 GB and Granite-4.2-30b 58.6 GB (no 4-bit repo found, do not fit). Note the three testable candidates are all one maker (Alibaba); Gemma 4 is Google. Not verified: vLLM 0.30 support for these, independent benchmarks, thinking-off behaviour. TEST QUEUED under the L587 rule: three Qwen NVFP4 builds on the 400 items, thinking off, local 5090, 0 USD; I compute the agreement scores.

PREDICTION Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4 (vLLM, thinking off, 400 items): 400/400 labelled, 0-4 parse failures, no truncation at 800 tokens, 15-30 items/s, about 100 output tokens per item, loads in under 32 GB.

CONTEXT7 CHECK (owner suggestion): Context7 holds docs, not leaderboards, so it gave benchmarks and serving facts but no candidate scores. FOUND (official docs pages): (1) benchmarks that match our task exist in EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness: JSONSchemaBench (paper 'Generating Structured Outputs from Language Models: Benchmark and Studies', arXiv 2501.10868) for strict JSON output, IFEval for verifiable instruction following, and LongProc (long procedures with structured outputs of 500 to 8,000 tokens) for long structured generation; no text-classification or extraction benchmark surfaced, so our own 400-item test stays the task benchmark. (2) vLLM stable docs list google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it as supported (Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration) and describe structured outputs with a JSON schema through StructuredOutputsParams(json=schema) using xgrammar; none of our local runs used constrained JSON (they parsed the final message), so constrained output is an untested option that could remove parse failures and change labels; the docs also state that online NVFP4 MoE quantization needs a Blackwell SM100 family GPU (the pre-quantized checkpoints we ran worked on the 5090). (3) Improvement loop: error signature, cluster by construction, bounded proposal with contrastive counterexamples, shadow evaluation on held-out data, promote only on predeclared gates, keep failures on the ledger; queue from unresolved cases, disagreements and conflicts plus a random audit of accepted high-confidence decisions; 'self-labels alone do not supply semantic truth' (same point as consistency is not correctness). PRESENCE MINING (600 devq items, Gemma vs Sonnet v3b A; 57 Sonnet-yes/Gemma-no, 49 Sonnet-no/Gemma-yes): misses are judgment calls on SIZE OF THE REAL-WORLD CHANGE FOR PEOPLE, not wording. Sonnet says yes to market-wide sell-off, 3,500 deaths from smoke, election violence fears with armed attacks, oil majors on record prices, city-wide hunger, 70,000-police protest warning, closure of a national newspaper. Sonnet says no to a single exchange hack (Binance), 62 layoffs at one factory, a 2.2% budget cut, two helicopters colliding, a malicious browser extension, one Azure bug. Gemma says yes to these small, single-organisation events. So the field is 'did a society-level condition change', and what separates yes from no is scale/breadth, which a text-only student sees only through a few hundred examples. Next ONE change: add a scale feature/head (people affected, breadth) trained on the existing 8k Sonnet rows' 'level' field, and score presence with a ranking metric (AUC, recall at precision 0.80) as for traits.

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).

Sonnet and Haiku come from one maker and share habits, so they count as one source; Qwen3-14B is the first independent maker (measured: same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on every field, L572).
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

notes: Only items dated after the 2026-10-25 training cutoff are scored. The first run on all 395 items was contaminated (story type 98%) and was discarded.
86 items means wide ranges (story type v5-leaf 85 to 97%). This shows direction, not a verdict.
Set is 69% real conditions, so Condition present: right is judged against always-yes.
Direction and size have under 12 scorable items and are not scored.

plain.blocker: Two things hold us up. (1) The better reader (v6b-student) is built and scored but not switched on. (2) Condition and its details are rare in a news feed and the labellers disagree on what counts, so more training cannot fix them: the definition has to change.

text: STEP 1 FINDING (own count from projects/world-state/runs/xtest/B1/runs/*_A_s0/results.jsonl, 597 items all four raters answered, presence variant A seed 0): 371 items get four no, 78 four yes, 148 split. Yes-rates differ by rater: Clef 34 percent, Jev 28, Qwen 19, Gemma 16. So much of the presence disagreement is a STRICTNESS threshold, not noise. Split items read: announced future closings (factory will close on a date, newspaper says it is shutting down), a credit-rating rise (a clear change, two raters said no), ongoing running counts. The rule text says 'already changed' and 'listed condition' but does not say whether an announced or in-progress event counts, or what a listed condition covers. Mapping = specs/topic_to_iptc_v1.json (written by us, not a published crosswalk), checked by lean/TopicMap.lean (49 guideline values, other excluded, every category reachable, at most three accepted categories per topic). Raters Clef, Gemma, Qwen local, 0 USD. SCORE: lenient accuracy (gold in accepted set) and strict accuracy (gold equals the first listed category), Wilson 95 percent, plus the best constant guess lenient rate on the same sample. PREDICTION: for every rater the lower end of lenient accuracy is at least 0.70 and at least 0.20 above the best constant guess; strict accuracy is reported, not gated. Failure is recorded against the mapping first (our own crosswalk), not against the raters, and per-category results decide which.

title: Field qualifier (triage) before labelling, presence first
text: Field qualifier (triage) before labelling, presence first
why: Owner 2026-11-04: define and qualify a field at the start, not at the end. Playbook 02 asks for a pilot and early agreement; the page has a Qualify stage but it ran after three presence codebooks. Source: MATTER cycle (Pustejovsky and Stubbs), pilot then revise before scaling.
acceptance: Gate written with a pre-set pass line per check, Lean file checks with no sorry, MM3 gate pass cited by run id.
Presence has a GO, REVISE or PARK outcome from the pilot, with n and 95 percent ranges, before any new labelling.
steps: Write the gate: 5 checks, GO or REVISE or PARK, in playbook
Lean the gate rule; MM3 front-run on the written gate
Presence: write definition lines, run a 100-item pilot
Apply the gate to presence and record the outcome

text: T32 CHECK 5 SHARPENED (owner 2026-11-04): evidence must be DIRECTLY in the input, first-order, actionable; second or third tier inference and background knowledge do not count. Operational test in the pilot: each rater quotes the supporting span; a second reader checks that the span alone states the answer; report the share of positives with a valid span and the share that needed inference; pass line fixed before the pilot. Failing check 1 (definable and measurable) or check 5 means PARK, because a better reader does not address those two (to be confirmed on the first parked field); failing only 2 or 3 means REVISE the definition, at most two rounds. The presence rule already excludes effects inferred from background knowledge (frozen v3b guideline); the share has not been measured yet. Gate order: 1 definable, 2 reliable (agreement above line, yes-rates within a band), 3 enough real cases, 4 outside anchor, 5 directly in the input.
