T32 engine card: BitMob Expert 1 v5-leaf

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

layers.asks: Pick something from the Pulse, such as a capability, and see what drives it, depends on it and is affected by it. Pilot done (L384): tags can be proposed on the CPU and verified by Clef, but agreement is only moderate, so the design is a hybrid.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: waiting for your yes (v5-leaf unchanged)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).

Sonnet and Haiku come from one maker and share habits, so they count as one source; Qwen3-14B is the first independent maker (measured: same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on every field, L572).

Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.

text: T31 engine card: BitMob Expert 1 v6b-student

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

DOC 00 REVIEW, EVIDENCE TEST 1 (playbook/00-knowledge-pipeline-v1.md section 13 and test T07: syndicated copies must not sit in both training and test). PRE-REGISTRATION: projects/world-state/leakage_check.py compares each of the 1500 sealed and 2000 DEVQ items against the 46775 training pool texts (data/pool_train.jsonl) and against each other, near-duplicate = Jaccard of word 4-gram shingles at least 0.8, or equal headline. PREDICTION: fewer than 2 percent of sealed items have a near-duplicate in the training pool, and fewer than 2 percent are near-duplicates of another sealed item. If higher, the sealed numbers of L771 are re-scored without the flagged items and both versions are reported; nothing is re-tuned.

DOC 00 REVIEW, EVIDENCE TEST 1 RESULT (runs/pulse/leakage_check.json, leakage_check.py): sealed 8 of 1500 = 0.0053 near-duplicate of a training pool text (8 share a headline), 4 of 1500 = 0.0027 duplicate within the set; DEVQ 34 of 2000 = 0.017 and 17 of 2000 = 0.0085. PREDICTION (under 2 percent each) HELD. Largest possible shift of the sealed scores of L771: 12 of 1499 = 0.8 points, so they stand; flagged ids kept in the file. EVIDENCE TEST 2 PRE-REGISTRATION (doc section 4: calibrated acceptance per head and abstention): projects/world-state/selective_check.py takes the v6b-student confidence for story type and for the two topic guesses, picks the lowest cutoff on DEVQ (1997 Sonnet labelled items) at which agreement among accepted items reaches 0.95, and applies that cutoff ONCE to the sealed set (1499) and to the fresh MN-DS articles (1600, topic two guesses against human labels, mapping v1). Also reports expected calibration error on DEVQ and sealed. PREDICTION: story type reaches 0.95 on DEVQ at coverage of at least 0.60, and on sealed the accepted share agrees at least 0.93; topic two guesses reaches 0.95 at coverage of at least 0.70, sealed accepted agreement at least 0.93; against human labels on MN-DS the accepted topic share is higher than the unfiltered 0.799 but below 0.95. No cutoff is chosen on sealed or MN-DS.

DOC 00 REVIEW, EVIDENCE TEST 2 RESULT (runs/pulse/selective_check.json, selective_check.py; cutoff from DEVQ only, applied once to sealed and MN-DS fresh). Story type: cutoff gives agreement 0.950 (0.939 to 0.959) at coverage 0.926 on DEVQ and 0.950 (0.937 to 0.960) at coverage 0.921 on sealed, against 0.919 and 0.916 unfiltered; calibration error 0.046 on both. Topic two guesses: cutoff 0.642 gives 0.950 at coverage 0.873 on DEVQ and 0.955 (0.942 to 0.965) at coverage 0.870 on sealed, against 0.915 and 0.922 unfiltered; calibration error 0.098 DEVQ and 0.093 sealed (the topic confidence is poorly calibrated). Against human labels (MN-DS fresh, mapping v1) the accepted 85.1 percent of articles agree 0.831 (0.810 to 0.850), against 0.799 for all. PREDICTIONS: all five HELD. READING under the Ready rule of L492 (a skipped item counts as a miss): abstention lowers the end to end rate (sealed topic 0.870 x 0.955 = 0.831 against 0.922 unfiltered; MN-DS 0.851 x 0.831 = 0.707), so it does not change any Ready verdict; what it adds is a CONFIDENT TIER the consumer can trust at 0.95 for about 87 to 92 percent of items, the same idea as the condition tiers of L486. DOC 00 REVIEW SUMMARY (playbook/00-knowledge-pipeline-v1.md, unchanged): it is a design for a larger system; Pulse maps to its G3 classification gate (heads Domain, Area, content function, conditions). Tools in it that our evidence reaches: (1) leakage check by group, tested, passes; (2) calibrated abstention, tested, gives a 0.95 tier, topic needs recalibration; (3) FACTUALITY as a separate label (Asserted, Reported, Planned, Predicted, Denied) on each fragment: our presence split items were announced and in progress events (L698) and MAVEN-FACT has human factuality labels, so presence can be split into a part with an outside anchor (did it happen) and a part without (is it a listed condition); not yet tested; (4) ADWIN style drift monitoring for per field agreement without halting, a gap noted at T27; (5) content function as multilabel instead of one story type, since opinion 0.61 and unclear 0.52 agree least (L744 era, Fit card), not yet tested. Out of scope for Pulse: Rust extractor and 1 ms scan, knowledge graph, ontology evolution, tenant isolation, answer engine.

T33 PRE-REGISTRATION. HYPOTHESES: H1 the rater disagreement on presence (alpha 0.580, yes-rate spread 0.182, L752) comes from the factuality part (did the change already happen); H2 it comes from the scope part (is it one of the 38 listed conditions). TEST: a new question in xtest/bundle.py, additive (field happened, yes or no, variants A and P): does this item state that at least one event has already taken place; yes = the item states a completed or in effect event, no = announced, planned, predicted, possible, denied or only proposed. Items: runs/xtest/items_T32r2.jsonl, 1552 = the 600 news items of B1 plus the 952 MAVEN-FACT sentences of T29. Raters Clef, Gemma, Qwen, local, 0 USD, seed 0, frozen v3b intro. MAVEN gold (data/anchors/maven_fact/gold_T29.json): yes = a sentence with at least one CT+ event (476), no = none (476); this is the happened concept of lean/MavenFactFit.lean (hasCertainEvent), scored two sided. PREDICTIONS: (1) every rater balanced accuracy on the MAVEN sentences at least 0.90; (2) on the 597 paired news items alpha over the three raters for happened at least 0.68 (presence alpha 0.580 plus 0.10) and the spread of yes-rates at most 0.10. READING RULE: (2) holds means H1 is supported and presence should be rebuilt as happened AND listed-condition with the first part anchored; (2) fails means the disagreement lives in the scope part (H2) and the next test is a scope question against the 38 condition definitions. Scope part has no outside anchor either way.

T33 ROUND 1 SCORE (pre-registered L785; runs/xtest/B10/score_t33.json from projects/world-state/score_t33.py; 1552 items, Clef Gemma Qwen, 0 USD). Question: does this item state that at least one event has already taken place. MAVEN-FACT two sided, yes recall and no recall: Clef 344 of 476 (0.723) and 313 of 476 (0.658), balanced 0.690; Gemma 471 of 476 (0.989) and 36 of 476 (0.076), balanced 0.533; Qwen 453 of 476 (0.952) and 158 of 476 (0.332), balanced 0.642. News items (597 paired): happened yes-rates Clef 0.663, Gemma 0.982, Qwen 0.953, spread 0.319, alpha 0.072 (0.010 to 0.144) against presence 0.580. Consistency: presence yes but happened no on 23 of 202 for Clef and 0 for Gemma and Qwen. PREDICTIONS: (1) balanced accuracy at least 0.90 for every rater FAILED; (2) alpha at least 0.68 and spread at most 0.10 FAILED. READING: my design error, not evidence about H1 or H2: at least one event is true of almost any news text (a statement or an announcement is itself an event), and the gold marks one specific annotated event, so the question did not measure the concept the gold labels; by playbook 13 check 1 this question was not definable as written. Doc 00 puts factuality on a fragment with a predicate span, not on the whole item. H1 versus H2 is NOT decided by this round. ROUND 2: per-event question with the trigger word marked, two sided against MAVEN-FACT per-event human labels.

T31 engine card: BitMob Expert 1 v6b-student

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).

Sonnet and Haiku come from one maker and share habits, so they count as one source; Qwen3-14B is the first independent maker (measured: same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on every field, L572).
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

86 items means wide ranges (story type v5-leaf 85 to 97%). This shows direction, not a verdict.

T33 ROUND 2 SCORE (pre-registered L788; runs/xtest/B11/score_t33b.json from projects/world-state/score_t33b.py; 1818 marked MAVEN-FACT validation events, 909 happened (CT+) and 909 not, human labels; Clef Gemma Qwen, 0 USD, no failures). Right when it happened: Clef 785 of 909 (0.864), Gemma 864 (0.950), Qwen 830 (0.913). Right when it did NOT happen: Clef 336 of 909 (0.370), Gemma 193 (0.212), Qwen 578 (0.636); by class Gemma CT- 54 of 384 (0.14), PS+ 128 of 453 (0.28); Qwen CT- 250 (0.65), PS+ 283 (0.62), PS- 40 of 52, Uu 5 of 20. Balanced accuracy Clef 0.617, Gemma 0.581, Qwen 0.774; majority vote of the three 0.643; alpha over the three 0.445 (0.409 to 0.479), all three agree on 0.689 of events. PREDICTIONS: (1) every rater balanced accuracy at least 0.85 FAILED; (2) alpha at least 0.70 FAILED. READING: factuality of a marked event is poorly judged zero shot by these three readers: they say it happened for most events and fail to say no for denied, planned or possible ones; the alpha of 0.445 is LOWER than combined presence (0.580, L752), so the disagreement does live at least partly in the factuality part (H1 supported in that sense, not decided against H2); the human labels the anchor provides are the way to train this part. Doc 00 puts factuality on a fragment: a supervised head is its route, not a better prompt. NEXT: feasibility of a small supervised factuality head on the human labelled validation events only (document grouped cross validation), internal research, no use of the train file whose licence and model assisted labels are unresolved.
T33 step 2 done

T33 STEP 3 PRE-REGISTRATION: supervised factuality head feasibility, projects/world-state/factuality_head_cv.py. Data: the 1818 marked human labelled validation events of T33 round 2 only (data/anchors/maven_fact/items_T33b.jsonl, gold_T33b.json), label happened = CT+. Features: the base leaf encoder embedding of the marked sentence (expert1_v5_leaf artefact, CPU), nothing else; classifier: balanced logistic regression, fixed C=1, no tuning; 5-fold cross validation GROUPED BY DOCUMENT so no sentence of a test document is seen in training. Internal feasibility research on CPU, 0 USD; the train file is not used (licence and model assisted labels unresolved). PREDICTION: pooled out-of-fold balanced accuracy between 0.70 and 0.85, above the best zero-shot reader on the same items (Qwen 0.774)? NO, expected at or below it; the question is whether a trained head on 1.8k examples gets near or above 0.85. PASS LINE: balanced accuracy at least 0.85 with the lower end of the 95 percent range at least 0.82. READING: pass means a CPU factuality head is feasible from human labels (anchored extractor without AI at serving); 0.70 to 0.85 means feasible only with more labels or a token-level feature (the train file, 70k events, after the licence is settled); below 0.70 means the encoder embedding alone does not carry the marked-event factuality.

T33 STEP 3 RESULT (pre-registered L805; runs/xtest/B11/factuality_head_cv.json, factuality_head_cv.py; 1818 human labelled validation events, 576 documents, 5 fold document grouped CV, base leaf embedding plus balanced logistic regression, CPU, 0 USD): recall happened 683 of 909 (0.751), recall not happened 619 of 909 (0.681), balanced accuracy 0.716 (0.696 to 0.737); by class CT+ 0.75, PS+ 0.59, CT- 0.77, PS- 0.90 (47 of 52), Uu 0.40 (8 of 20). Pass line 0.85 MISSED; prediction band 0.70 to 0.85 HELD. Above Clef 0.617 and Gemma 0.581 zero shot, below Qwen 0.774 zero shot on the same items. CHANGE-CONTROL ROUND 2 (one change): add sparse features of the words within 4 tokens either side of the marked trigger (word 1 and 2 grams, trigger replaced by a marker), the doc 00 predicate window idea; everything else identical. PREDICTION: balanced accuracy at least 0.78 and lower end of the range above 0.74; pass line unchanged at 0.85 with lower end 0.82. If it misses 0.78 the embedding plus window route is closed at this label count and the next lever is the 70k train events after the licence is settled by the owner.
T33 step 3 done
Factuality tested on CPU raters (alpha 0.445, balanced 0.58 to 0.77) and a supervised head (0.804); H1 supported, path recorded

T33 STEP 3 ROUND 2 RESULT (pre-registered L806; runs/xtest/B11/factuality_head_cv_window.json, factuality_head_cv.py with WINDOW=4; the no-window baseline reproduced 0.716 in the same run): adding word 1 and 2 grams of the 4 tokens either side of the marked trigger gives balanced accuracy 0.804 (0.786 to 0.822), recall happened 757 of 909 (0.833), recall not happened 705 of 909 (0.776); by class CT+ 0.83, PS+ 0.74, CT- 0.84, PS- 0.92 (48 of 52), Uu 0.15 (3 of 20). PREDICTION at least 0.78 with lower end above 0.74: HELD; pass line 0.85 with lower end 0.82: MISSED. A CPU head trained on 1818 human labelled events beats the best zero shot reader (Qwen 0.774) and Clef and Gemma (0.617, 0.581). CONCLUSIONS: (1) factuality of a marked event IS extractable on CPU from human labels without AI at serving, and has an outside anchor; (2) it needs the trigger: a free text item has no marked trigger, so presence from this route needs an event detector first (doc 00 G2 solver) and a listed-condition head, whose scope part has no outside anchor; (3) next lever for the head is more human labels: the 70k event train file of MAVEN-FACT, which has an unstated licence and GPT-3.5 pre-annotation, OWNER DECISION: may it be used for training (internal research) or only for scoring; (4) Uu stays weak (20 examples). Presence stays parked (L758); this is the research path from it, not a verdict change.

T30 ANCHOR FOUND AND PRE-REGISTRATION: CLEF 2025 CheckThat! Task 1 subjectivity, English, Hugging Face mirror AIWizards/clef2025_checkthat_task1_subjectivity, licence stated in the card and shipped as legal text: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, share alike): INTERNAL SCORING ONLY, no training, no redistribution, folder data/anchors/checkthat_subj (git-ignored). 2076 labelled English sentences (train 830, dev 462, dev_test 484, test 300; OBJ 1331, SUBJ 745), annotator alpha 0.83 per the 2023 overview paper. Construct: objective versus subjective at SENTENCE level, which is not our four story types and not headline plus teaser. MAPPING (fixed now): primary SUBJ means v6b-student story type is opinion; secondary SUBJ means opinion or unclear; OBJ otherwise. Raters: v6b-student (CPU) and Clef. PREDICTIONS: OBJ recall at least 0.85; SUBJ recall between 0.20 and 0.60 (our opinion class is narrower than subjective: loaded wording is subjective but not an opinion); balanced accuracy between 0.58 and 0.75. READING: a balanced accuracy lower end of at least 0.70 means the fact versus opinion boundary has outside support; below that is expected because subjectivity is a wider construct, so a miss is reported as a construct gap and not as a failure of story type; forecast and unclear stay without an anchor.

T30 CHECKTHAT SCORE (pre-registered L810; runs/pulse/anchor_checkthat_v6b-student.json, score_checkthat.py; Clef via runs/xtest/B12; 2076 English sentences, internal scoring only, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). Primary mapping SUBJ means opinion: v6b-student subjective recall 468 of 745 (0.628), objective recall 985 of 1331 (0.740), balanced accuracy 0.684 (0.663 to 0.705); Clef 443 of 745 (0.595) and 997 of 1331 (0.749), balanced 0.672 (0.651 to 0.693). PREDICTIONS: objective recall at least 0.85 FAILED (0.740); subjective recall 0.20 to 0.60 narrowly MISSED for v6b-student (0.628) and held for Clef (0.595); balanced accuracy 0.58 to 0.75 HELD for both. Lower end 0.70 not reached by either, so the fact versus opinion boundary has only partial outside support; both readers behave alike (26 percent of objective sentences called opinion by v6b-student, 346 of 1331), so the ceiling here comes from the construct (subjective is wider than opinion) and the domain (sentences, opinion heavy sources), not from reader size. STEP 2 PRE-REGISTRATION, own checkable test for forecast (one sided, it can refute a forecast call and never confirm one, as in lean/MavenFactFit.lean): projects/world-state/forecast_cue_test.py counts, among the sealed items v6b-student calls forecast, the share whose text holds a future cue (will, would, expected to, forecast, projected, predicts, likely to, set to, plans to, poised to, could, may, might, a year in the future, next year or month or week, in the coming, outlook). PREDICTION: at least 0.90 of v6b-student forecast calls hold a cue; Sonnet forecast labels of the same items hold a cue at least 0.90 too; the share of cue-free forecast calls is listed in full.

PREDICTION (both at least 0.90) FAILED. T39 PRE-REGISTRATION (topic confidence recalibration; engine NOT changed, a calibration map is produced and scored, wiring it in is an engine change for later). Method: isotonic regression from the v6b-student topic two guess confidence to hit or miss, fitted on DEVQ only (1997 Sonnet labelled items), applied once to sealed (1499); expected calibration error with 10 equal width bins, measured before and after. Script projects/world-state/calibrate_topic.py, map saved to runs/pulse/topic_calibration.json. PREDICTION: calibration error falls from 0.098 on DEVQ and 0.093 on sealed (L782) to under 0.05 on sealed; the accepted share at the DEVQ 0.95 cutoff changes by less than 0.03 coverage. If sealed stays at 0.05 or more the topic confidence stays flagged.

T39 RESULT (pre-registered L823; runs/pulse/topic_calibration.json, projects/world-state/calibrate_topic.py; isotonic map fitted on DEVQ only; engine NOT changed). Against Sonnet agreement: calibration error on sealed 0.093 before and 0.013 after (target under 0.05: HELD; DEVQ is in sample so its 0.0 is not evidence); mean confidence 0.829 against hit rate 0.922 before, 0.920 after, i.e. the raw topic confidence is underconfident against Sonnet. Coverage change at the 0.95 cutoff was not measured; the map is monotone so the order of items is unchanged. SAME MAP AGAINST HUMAN LABELS (MN-DS fresh, 1600 articles, lenient hit): raw confidence mean 0.808 against hit rate 0.799, calibration error 0.073; calibrated to Sonnet mean 0.907, error 0.113. READING: the raw topic confidence is already close to honest against the human labels and the Sonnet calibrated one overstates them by about 0.11; a calibration target must follow the governing bar, and Sonnet agreement runs higher than the outside check on the same items (0.922 sealed against 0.799 MN-DS, different samples and an unequal taxonomy). RECOMMENDATION recorded as default, the owner can change it: report two numbers to consumers, agreement with the teacher (Ready rule L492, governs Ready) and the outside check (caveat, topic sits at the 0.80 line, point 0.799, low end 0.779); do NOT ship the Sonnet calibrated map as a confidence. Steps 1 and 2 done; step 3 (which bar governs, an owner decision) stays open.

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

fitness.name: Field checks v2
fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?
measures.m: Krippendorff's alpha: agreement beyond chance (1 = perfect, 0 = no better than guessing)

measures.q: Does agreement hold when a model from a different maker (Qwen3-14B) votes with Sonnet and Haiku?
measures.m: alpha over Sonnet, Haiku (one maker) and Qwen on the 395 items
measures.bar: same bands as the agreement score; a flag only, it does not change the verdict

measures.q: Does each answer agree, the rare ones too?
Do Sonnet and Haiku agree, not just each with itself? Same maker, so this is not an independent check.
How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?
measures.bar: ours: 10% or less ok · over 20% fail

measures.q: Does one model repeat itself?
measures.cite: none found (stability is not correctness: arXiv 2609.15194)

fit_tests.q: Would careful readers give the same answer?
fit_tests.m: the Agreement score above
fit_tests.bar: same bands as agreement score

fit_tests.q: Does every answer have enough cases to learn and to score?
fit_tests.m: cases per answer on the 395 four-vote items (the full labelled pool is larger, with one voter)
fit_tests.bar: ours: 30+ per answer; under that the answer needs targeted data
fit_tests.cite: LESSONS #8 (our notes); Graham & Bull 1998 uses 200+ for intervals

fit_tests.q: Is there trusted outside labelled data?
fit_tests.m: named outside dataset for the field
fit_tests.bar: none = agreement only: the field can never be called correct
fit_tests.src: our design; datasets named in playbook 01

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread.
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.
next.ask: adopt v6b-student (sealed check first) · capability sources · tags at serving

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

fitness.name: Field checks v2
fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?
measures.m: Krippendorff's alpha: agreement beyond chance (1 = perfect, 0 = no better than guessing)

measures.q: Does agreement hold when a model from a different maker (Qwen3-14B) votes with Sonnet and Haiku?
measures.m: alpha over Sonnet, Haiku (one maker) and Qwen on the 395 items
measures.bar: same bands as the agreement score; a flag only, it does not change the verdict

measures.q: Does each answer agree, the rare ones too?
Do Sonnet and Haiku agree, not just each with itself? Same maker, so this is not an independent check.
How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?
measures.bar: ours: 10% or less ok · over 20% fail

measures.q: Does one model repeat itself?
measures.cite: none found (stability is not correctness: arXiv 2609.15194)

fit_tests.m: the Agreement score above
fit_tests.bar: same bands as agreement score

fit_tests.q: Does every answer have enough cases to learn and to score?

fit_tests.bar: ours: 30+ per answer; under that the answer needs targeted data
fit_tests.cite: LESSONS #8 (our notes); Graham & Bull 1998 uses 200+ for intervals

fit_tests.bar: none = agreement only: the field can never be called correct

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).

Sonnet and Haiku come from one maker and share habits, so they count as one source; Qwen3-14B is the first independent maker (measured: same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on every field, L572).
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

fitness.name: Field checks v2
fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?
measures.m: Krippendorff's alpha: agreement beyond chance (1 = perfect, 0 = no better than guessing)

measures.q: Does agreement hold when a model from a different maker (Qwen3-14B) votes with Sonnet and Haiku?
measures.m: alpha over Sonnet, Haiku (one maker) and Qwen on the 395 items
measures.bar: same bands as the agreement score; a flag only, it does not change the verdict

measures.q: Does each answer agree, the rare ones too?
Do Sonnet and Haiku agree, not just each with itself? Same maker, so this is not an independent check.
How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?
measures.bar: ours: 10% or less ok · over 20% fail

measures.q: Does one model repeat itself?
measures.cite: none found (stability is not correctness: arXiv 2609.15194)

fit_tests.q: Would careful readers give the same answer?
fit_tests.m: the Agreement score above
fit_tests.bar: same bands as agreement score

fit_tests.q: Does every answer have enough cases to learn and to score?
fit_tests.m: cases per answer on the 395 four-vote items (the full labelled pool is larger, with one voter)
fit_tests.bar: ours: 30+ per answer; under that the answer needs targeted data
fit_tests.cite: LESSONS #8 (our notes); Graham & Bull 1998 uses 200+ for intervals

fit_tests.q: Is there trusted outside labelled data?
fit_tests.m: named outside dataset for the field
fit_tests.bar: none = agreement only: the field can never be called correct
fit_tests.src: our design; datasets named in playbook 01

fit_tests.q: Does the headline plus description carry the evidence?
fit_tests.m: agreement between headline-only and full-article labels
fit_tests.bar: not measured yet

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).

Sonnet and Haiku come from one maker and share habits, so they count as one source; Qwen3-14B is the first independent maker (measured: same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on every field, L572).
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

notes: Only items dated after the 2026-10-25 training cutoff are scored. The first run on all 395 items was contaminated (story type 98%) and was discarded.
86 items means wide ranges (story type v5-leaf 85 to 97%). This shows direction, not a verdict.
Set is 69% real conditions, so Condition present: right is judged against always-yes.
Direction and size have under 12 scorable items and are not scored.

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread. From 2026-11-05 the same reader also serves per-condition heads for four kinds (air pollution, biodiversity loss, civil unrest, cyber insecurity) and a direction head for biodiversity loss, on the same embedding, 16.6 ms median over HTTP (service pulse_reader, route /v1/pulse; nothing calls it yet).
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

text: Pre-registration, T37 pooled labeller heads (projects/world-state/perkind_pooled.py). Hypothesis: a head trained on BOTH labellers (each item contributes one row per labeller that labelled it, weight 0.5 when both did, weight 1 when one did) holds up against each labeller separately. Design: the 18791 items both labelled are split 70 percent train and 30 percent test (seed 0); training also uses the 27801 Haiku only items and the Sonnet only items with texts; threshold from a 20 percent hold of the training rows; test = the 30 percent both labelled items, scored separately against Sonnet and against Haiku. 16 kinds as before. Pass per kind: F1 vs Sonnet and F1 vs Haiku both at least the Sonnet vs Haiku F1 minus 0.05 (the both directions rule of L893). Prediction: at least 8 of 16 pass (probability 0.5); the 4 kinds of L894 are expected to pass again. A kind that passes becomes a candidate for a per kind field; the owner must still agree to the contract.

T37 POOLED LABELLER HEADS SCORED (pre-registered L904; projects/world-state/perkind_pooled.py, runs/pulse/perkind_pooled.json; trained on both labellers, tested on a 30 percent part of the 18791 items both labelled, scored against Sonnet and Haiku separately, 0 USD; first launch crashed on an empty label set, fixed with one line and rerun, no result seen before the fix). PREDICTION (at least 8): MISSED. biodiversity_loss misses by 0.001 (F1 vs Haiku 0.606 against the line 0.607). ACROSS THE THREE DESIGNS (L892 Sonnet trained scored vs Haiku, L894 Haiku trained scored vs Sonnet, this pooled test): air_pollution, civil_unrest and cyber_insecurity pass all three; biodiversity_loss, disruption and job_security pass two of three; the other ten kinds pass at most one design. The served heads (L900) cover air_pollution, civil_unrest, cyber_insecurity and biodiversity_loss; the biodiversity_loss head is the least supported of the four and the fact sheet should say it passed two of three designs. Next: put that line on the fact sheet and the card.

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread. From 2026-11-05 the same reader also serves per-condition heads for four kinds (air pollution, biodiversity loss, civil unrest, cyber insecurity) and a direction head for biodiversity loss, on the same embedding, 16.6 ms median over HTTP (service pulse_reader, route /v1/pulse; nothing calls it yet).
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built.

next.headline: Adopt v6b-student? Passes story type; condition detection still not ready.
next.body: Under the new Ready rule (counted over every item, and it must beat always guessing the common answer): today's engine passes on topic only. Story type is 87.5% against 87.0% for always saying 'fact', so it is not proven to add anything. v6b-student passes on story type (91.8%, low end 90.3%, against 85.2% for guessing) and on topic. Neither version passes condition detection: v6b finds 33% of real conditions (needs 80%), and its yes/no on 'is there a condition' (86.7%) is still under the 89.6% you get by always saying no. Measured on 1,593 fresh items it never saw; agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Nothing has been replaced yet.

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

fitness.name: Field checks v2
fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?
measures.m: Krippendorff's alpha: agreement beyond chance (1 = perfect, 0 = no better than guessing)

Do Sonnet and Haiku agree, not just each with itself? Same maker, so this is not an independent check.
How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?

measures.q: Does one model repeat itself?
