items.what: Training the student on d1's soft labels
items.result: Topic top-2 -0.008, story -0.006, which-condition +0.009 to +0.02
items.outcome: No gain; d1 stays a live second opinion

tried_groups.name: Free-form tags (pilot: 100 articles, 100 headline items)
tried_groups.summary: CPU proposes, Clef verifies: about 3 tags per headline item, 5.4 per full article; wording agreement about 0.5; 77% of tags occur once. Capabilities are 7% of general-news tags and 23% of tech-news tags, and almost never recur across articles: news can propose capability candidates but cannot supply the capability layer. Design: a hybrid.

items.what: Tag pilot with spaCy proposer and local Clef verifier (5 narrow yes/no questions per candidate)
items.result: 41% of 2,762 candidates accepted; kappa 0.49 to 0.53; merge at cosine 0.80 cuts distinct tags by 33% but merges related, not only identical, tags; 56% of full-article tags are absent from the short version
items.outcome: Hybrid design; capability layer needs tech sources; a token-level tag head is the serving route (the proposer takes 0.7 s per item)

changes.title: Fresh-slice check, a CPU condition-presence head, and a teacher instability
changes.text: Fresh MN-DS slice scored once (1,545 articles, human labels): all articles 78.5%; threshold 700 answers 67.5% at 82.7%, 500 answers 92.9% at 79.5%, just under the 0.80 line, so the setting stays at 700 (an advisor suggestion to set 500 was not followed; ledger L1176). A condition-presence sparse head on CPU scores F1 0.64 against Sonnet on the sealed set (always saying yes: 0.20). The agreement claims stand against their base rates (story type 91.5% against always-fact 84.5%). Two more teacher batches found conditions in 4.9% of 494 gists against 10.4% in the first 250, so the teacher's condition call depends on who reads it; fix the definition before training on it. Ledger L1175 to L1178.

changes.title: Condition test on a working definition: the change lexicon is a proposer, not an answer
changes.text: A teacher batch of 250 gists, picked from the rebalanced pool, gave 26 with a condition (10.4%), against 1.6% in the first 1,000. The change lexicon proposed a condition for 239 of the 250 and the teacher confirmed 23 (precision 9.6%); its proposals cover 88.5% of the teacher's conditions. Good for choosing articles to label, unfit as an answer. The rise from 1.6% is not credited to the proposals alone: the topic mix changed too. Working definition (a thing, a kind and a direction already changed), not a confirmed contract. Ledger L1171, L1172.

changes.title: Sparse heads can answer first and skip the encoder (behind a switch, off by default)
changes.text: A sparse topic head and a sparse story-type head, trained on Sonnet labels only, answer when both are confident and the encoder is skipped. Topic against human labels: chain 79.8% with the sparse head answering half, against 79.9% for v6b alone. On 200 full articles the encoder is skipped for 22.0% and the median time falls from 75.0 to 60.5 ms with the same answers. Whole chain on 1,600 human-labelled articles: 79.3% off, 79.5% on. Weak on forecast and opinion, so v6b still carries those. Ledger L1119, L1134, L1137, L1147.

changes.title: The toolchain read 20,000 articles in 243 seconds
changes.text: Every article through the scan, span rules, fact extractors, name finder, place linker, factuality tagger and change lexicon, each item stored with its strength: 92.0% of articles have at least one amount or date that passed all four checks (strength proved); everything else is rule. Ledger L1144, L1145.

changes.title: Triples find events the fact extractors miss; negation from triples helps the factuality tagger
changes.text: Against 6,029 human-marked events the open-extraction triples find the event word in 87.9%, the extractors' who-did-what in 72.6%; keep both. Taking certain, negated or possible from the triples lifts the factuality tagger's balanced accuracy from 0.4716 to 0.5428 and negated events caught from 17 to 46 of 151. Ledger L1129, L1143.

changes.title: Boilerplate strip and a retrain with 1,000 teacher labels moved nothing
changes.text: Boilerplate strip changed 0 of 36,092 training texts (labelled texts have no line breaks) and left the topic score at 75.5%. The sparse heads refit with 1,000 weak gist labels: topic 75.4% against 75.5%; the new rows are 2.7% of the training set. The teacher reading only the gist agrees with its full-article label on 83.0% of topics and 94.0% of story types (100 articles, same teacher). Ledger L1133, L1156, L1157.

changes.title: Topic confidence threshold: a coverage choice, not a tuning win
changes.text: At threshold 700 the decider answers topic on 60.6% of articles at 83.1% right against human labels; the withheld 39.4% are still 73.5% right. At 500 it answers 89.7% at 81.3%. A split-half test chose 300 on one half and 500 on the other, so confidence separates right from wrong only weakly. Not applied; the owner chooses. Ledger L1149, L1162.

changes.title: Wiring the sparse heads was first 21 times slower
changes.text: One scikit-learn probability call on a single sparse row took 1.5 s; the same sums as one matrix product take 0.08 ms and match to 6e-07. Fixed and rerun. Ledger L1136, L1137.

changes.title: Amounts, dates, names and triples now have a validator
changes.text: Stated facts are checked against the text itself, not against labellers: amounts pass all four checks 97.5%, dates 90.9%, names 40.7% (most names are modifiers and stay unbound), complete subject-verb-object triples 49.7% of fragments. Two flaws found and fixed while measuring (the scanner hid dates inside names; a date's day number counted as an amount). Ledger L958, L959.

changes.title: Direction and size taken off the condition chain
changes.text: They sat as 'blocked until condition is ready' for days. Now each is scored on its own: direction learned from the story text reaches 84.2% over every story against 78.4% for always up (falls 77% found, 80% needed); size is read as the stated amount, found in 27% of condition stories and 98% a real quantity. Ledger L951 to L954, L932.

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

fitness.name: Field checks v2
fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?
measures.m: Krippendorff's alpha: agreement beyond chance (1 = perfect, 0 = no better than guessing)

measures.q: Does agreement hold when a model from a different maker (Qwen3-14B) votes with Sonnet and Haiku?
measures.m: alpha over Sonnet, Haiku (one maker) and Qwen on the 395 items
measures.bar: same bands as the agreement score; a flag only, it does not change the verdict

measures.q: Does each answer agree, the rare ones too?
Do Sonnet and Haiku agree, not just each with itself? Same maker, so this is not an independent check.
How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?
measures.bar: ours: 10% or less ok · over 20% fail

measures.q: Does one model repeat itself?
measures.cite: none found (stability is not correctness: arXiv 2609.15194)

fit_tests.q: Would careful readers give the same answer?

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).

Sonnet and Haiku come from one maker and share habits, so they count as one source; Qwen3-14B is the first independent maker (measured: same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on every field, L572).
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

notes: Only items dated after the 2026-10-25 training cutoff are scored. The first run on all 395 items was contaminated (story type 98%) and was discarded.
86 items means wide ranges (story type v5-leaf 85 to 97%). This shows direction, not a verdict.
Set is 69% real conditions, so Condition present: right is judged against always-yes.
Direction and size have under 12 scorable items and are not scored.

plain.blocker: Story type and topic are ready; the reader that serves them is v6b-student (15 ms, one CPU thread). Condition is parked: the CPU reader finds about 3 in 10 real cases. Direction and size no longer wait behind it: direction is learned from the story at 84.2% (guessing up: 78.4%), size is read as the stated amount (found in 27% of condition stories, 98% a real quantity).

rows.line: Sealed set: 91.5% agreement with Sonnet (90.0% to 92.8%), always saying 'fact' gets 84.5%. No outside anchor yet (T30). Held back by the decider: the contract is not confirmed and CheckThat scores fact versus opinion, not our four types (field table).

Two guesses: 92.2% agreement with Sonnet on the sealed set (best constant pair 38.2%); 79.9% against human labels (MN-DS, fresh articles), right at the 80% line. Whole chain on the human labels: 79.3% with the sparse heads off, 79.5% on; the decider answers 60.6% of articles (threshold 700).
Parked at the field gate after two definition rounds. v6b-student finds 29.3% of real cases and its end-to-end 86.3% is below simply saying no (89.1%). No gross false-yes errors in the outside check.
Only meaningful on articles that have a condition. 79.2%, 3 points short.
Learned from the story on its own: right 84.2% over 3,871 stories against 78.4% for always up; finds 77% of real falls (80% needed). Agreement with Sonnet, not outside truth (L954).

Read as the stated amount and checked against the text: 97.5% of 5,323 amounts pass all four checks (in the text, value reads back, bound to a noun or verb, one sentence). Spot check: 87% are the condition's own. Replaces small / notable / large. Stated is not true (L959). Held back by the decider until its contract is confirmed.

Counted per trait, not one pass or fail: 2 of 51 traits are GO (deaths or injuries; a household price went up, revised wording). Two others failed the gate (a threat to the natural environment, a single city or smaller area). 45 need a wording revision, 2 need more positive examples. The row is Ready when you name the traits the product needs and all of them are GO.

text: CORRECTION (computed from /workspace/demo/mockups/gates/data.json): my reports in this session that the Reading gates rounds table showed R5, M1, M3 and the base-rate row were wrong. Scripted edits to gates_heads.py used replace calls that matched nothing, so the table held five rounds until now. Fixed with asserted edits: it now holds ten (R1, R2, R3, Exit, Finding, R5, M1, M2, M3, Base), and the stale lap-two statuses (topic setting, teacher labels, score, status line, Condition training row) are updated and read back from data.json. The Engine card was built separately and did carry M1, M2 and M3 (L1173, L1179). The fake-DOM test renders the table; both pages read OK in monitor_pages. Lesson filed in LESSONS_LEARNED.md.

PREDICTIONS lap two, two free tests (the main session proceeding on working defaults; the Opus advisor memo asked for a fresh slice, and the condition instability in L1178 asks for a stability test). TEST S: 100 items (50 the earlier labellers gave a condition and 50 they did not, seeded, from the 744 gists) are labelled for the conditions field by four independent Sonnet agents on session tokens: two under the registered prompt and two under a sharper rule A (the change has already happened, the thing and kind are named, the direction is clear, all in the item's own words, empty when in doubt; file runs/harvest/pool_v2/rubric_A.txt). Measure: Cohen kappa on whether an item has a condition, between the two agents of each pair, and the share of both-yes items where kind and direction also match. Predicted: kappa under the registered prompt between 0.30 and 0.60; kappa under rule A at least 0.10 higher; condition share under rule A lower than under the registered prompt. Judge: agreement between labellers (stability), not outside truth. TEST F: a second fresh MN-DS slice (rows not in T28, T28b or the first fresh slice, 100 per category, seeded) is scored once with the whole chain at topic thresholds 500, 600 and 700. Predicted: at 700 answered 0.60 to 0.72 at accuracy 0.80 to 0.85; at 600 answered 0.77 to 0.88 at accuracy 0.79 to 0.83; at 500 answered 0.88 to 0.95 at accuracy 0.77 to 0.82. Reason (estimate): on the first fresh slice the answered set at the middle setting was right at the rate below (src: /workspace/knowledge_pipeline/projects/world-state/runs/pulse/m1_fresh.json#thr_700.answered_acc), and the curve for the other two settings is in the same file. Purpose of F: 600 was read off the first slice, so it needs a clean slice before it can be recommended.

SCORE test S (computed, prediction L1181, src: /workspace/knowledge_pipeline/projects/world-state/runs/pulse/stability_test.json#registered_pair_S1_S2.kappa): on the same 100 items (half picked from earlier labelled positives, so shares are not base rates), two independent Sonnet labellers under the registered prompt agree on whether an item has a condition with Cohen kappa 0.80, range 0.67 to 0.92, and match kind and direction on every item where both said yes. Under the sharper rule A the two labellers reach kappa 0.72, range 0.57 to 0.84 (src: same file#ruleA_pair_R1_R2.kappa). Predicted kappa 0.30 to 0.60 under the registered prompt: MISS, above; predicted rule A at least 0.10 higher than the registered prompt: MISS (it is 0.08 lower, inside the ranges); condition share lower under rule A: HIT by a small margin (0.40 and 0.50 against 0.51 and 0.45). CORRECTION to L1178, to the lap-two status line and to the Engine card: I wrote that the teacher's condition call depends on which labeller reads the item (10.4, 4.0 and 5.7 percent across three batches) and that the definition should be fixed before training on the labels. This test does not support that: independent labellers agree on the same items, so the batch-to-batch differences come from the items and from sampling (26 of 250 against a pooled 6.7 percent is about 2.3 standard errors high), not from labeller instability. Rule A does not help and is dropped. Caveats: both labellers are the same model family and agree partly through shared habits; this is agreement, not outside truth. Effect on the Condition decision: labeller agreement is not the blocker; the owner's confirmation of the definition and the thin count (50 conditions in 744 gists) are.
T42 engine card: BitMob Expert 1 v6b-student

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread. From 2026-11-05 the same reader also serves per-condition heads for four kinds (air pollution, biodiversity loss, civil unrest, cyber insecurity) and a direction head for biodiversity loss, on the same embedding, 16.6 ms median over HTTP (service pulse_reader, route /v1/pulse; nothing calls it yet). Since 2026-11-08 an optional pair of sparse heads (topic and story type) can answer first and skip the encoder when both are confident; off by default (ledger L1137).
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built. Exception (owner, 2026-11-05): direction and size are read from the story text and scored on their own; they do not wait on condition.

layers.name: Macro / Pulse
layers.asks: What is changing, and where? One expert reads each item once and answers all of these.

fields.label: Story type
fields.what: Fact, forecast, opinion or unclear
fields.work: v6b-student 91.5% on the sealed set (always saying 'fact': 84.5%)
fields.step: Outside anchor for fact vs opinion (T30)

fit.why: Agreement score 0.695 sits between Krippendorff's 0.667 and 0.80, so conclusions are tentative. 'Fact' agrees 97% but opinion 61% and unclear 52% (the 20-vote bar for a rare answer is ours).
fit.fix: Rewrite the opinion and unclear rules, re-vote, and see whether agreement score reaches 0.80.

f2.t: 3 of 4 answers under 30 cases (rarest: unclear 1, opinion 8, forecast 16)

fields.label: Topic
fields.what: One of 49 topics, two guesses
fields.work: v6b-student 92.2% with two guesses on the sealed set (best constant pair: 38.2%); 79.9% against human labels
fields.bad: Voters split on 1 in 8 items
fields.step: Decide which bar governs: Sonnet agreement or human labels

fit.why: Agreement score 0.89 is above 0.80. The weakest topic, governance_corruption, agrees 70%.
fit.fix: Nothing to fix before training. Open question: a trusted outside label set (F3).

f2.t: 46 of 47 answers under 30 cases (rarest: media_information 1, technology_consumer 1, courts_rulings 1)

fields.label: Condition present
fields.what: Does the story report a change in one of 38 world conditions
fields.work: Union of 38 stays parked: v6b-student finds 29.3% of real conditions (0.80 needed). New: one narrow head per kind, tested three ways against two Claude labellers (L892, L894, L905). Air pollution, civil unrest and cyber insecurity pass all three; biodiversity loss, disruption and job security pass two of three; the other ten pass at most one
fields.bad: Finds 1 in 5 real cases; voters agree on only 68%
fields.step: Offer air pollution, civil unrest, cyber insecurity as per-kind fields; biodiversity loss is served but passed two of three (missed one by 0.001). Contract change needs the owner. No outside truth set found (L896)

fit.why: Agreement score 0.50 is under 0.667: labellers do not agree beyond chance. Sonnet says yes 49% of the time, Haiku 67%, and Clef cannot arbitrate (57% on the split items).
fit.fix: Rewrite the rule (a condition counts only if the story reports it changed), re-vote, re-measure. If agreement score stays under 0.667, drop it or make it two-tier.

f2.t: all 2 answers have 30+ cases

fields.label: Which condition (of real cases)
fields.what: Its top pick for every real condition, no confidence gate (the honest version of the row above)
fields.work: Waits on condition. v6b-student on the sealed set, given a found condition: 95.8% (n 48); too few cases to call it ready
fields.bad: 79.2%, 3 pts short
fields.step: Adopt v6b: 82.7% (decision 1)

fit.why: Agreement score 0.913 is above 0.80: the labels are clean.
fit.fix: The stall is elsewhere: too few real cases for most conditions (F2) and model capacity.

f2.t: 35 of 35 answers under 30 cases (rarest: tech_adoption 1, mental_distress 1, information_reliability 1)

fields.label: Direction (read from the story)
fields.what: Up or down, learned from the story text on its own. It no longer waits on condition (owner, 2026-11-05).
fields.work: Trained CPU head on its own over 3,871 stories: right 84.2% over every story against 78.4% for always saying up; finds 77% of real falls (80% needed), 61% of its fall calls are right. Counting change words by hand is no better than guessing (78.2%). Sonnet and Haiku agree on direction 97.4% of the time. Agreement with Sonnet, not outside truth (L952, L954).
fields.bad: Falls are the hard side: it misses about 1 in 4 real falls and 4 in 10 of its fall calls are wrong
fields.step: Read direction together with the thing that changes (the fragment it sits in), then re-test against the 80% bar for falls

fit.why: Agreement score 0.945 is above 0.80.
fit.fix: Nothing to fix. Check F3 (outside label set) before calling it correct.

f2.t: all 2 answers have 30+ cases

fields.label: Size (the stated amount)
fields.what: The amount the story itself states: a number with its unit and what it counts. Blank when the story states none. It no longer waits on condition.
fields.work: Read as the stated amount, checked against the story text itself: 97.5% of the 5,323 amounts found in 4,102 condition stories pass all four checks (span is in the text, the value reads back, bound to a counted noun or verb, inside one sentence); 2.5% are left unbound. Earlier spot check of 100 by one reader: 98% real quantities, 87% the condition's own amount (L932). A different contract from small / notable / large, which two Claude labellers agreed on only 43% to 68% of the time (L895). Stated is not true: it checks what the text says (L959).
fields.bad: Whether the amount belongs to the condition (not a subsidy or a police deployment) is still only spot-checked, 13 in 100 belonged to something else
fields.step: Tie the amount to its who-did-what fragment so it is the condition's own; owner to confirm this replaces small / notable / large (T38)

fit.why: Agreement shown is for the old small / notable / large labels, kept for the record. The stated-amount contract is checked against the story text itself, not against labellers.
fit.fix: Decide whether exact steps matter. If so, the exact-step measure needs your yes.

f2.t: 1 of 4 answers under 30 cases (rarest: severe 2)

fields.label: Traits (51 questions, 8 groups)
fields.what: 51 questions in 8 groups. Not built into the engine yet. Tested on the CPU reader as present/absent flags: 24 of 51 questions usable (find half of present cases at 80% right); strongest groups scale (6 of 6) and intent (5 of 8). Graded answers (slightly / clearly / strongly) are not ready: 2 of 51.
fields.work: 3 of 51 traits GO (deaths or injuries, household prices up, shortage of a basic need); 1 GO-pending (cyber threat, wording judged weak on evidence); 13 parked after their allowed rounds; 34 untouched since the first gate
fields.bad: Agreement among three local models, no outside truth; the 3 GO traits are rare or narrow (shortage fires on about 1.4% of items)
fields.step: Owner names which traits the product needs (default L820); no further rounds on the abstract ones until then

layers.name: Area (drill into one thing)
layers.asks: Pick something from the Pulse, such as a capability, and see what drives it, depends on it and is affected by it. Pilot done (L384): tags can be proposed on the CPU and verified by Clef, but agreement is only moderate, so the design is a hybrid.

fields.label: Things and capabilities
fields.what: Find entities, places, concepts and capabilities in the item and link each to one stable identity. Pilot: about 5 tags per full article, 3 per headline item; reading the whole article adds 56% new tags.

fields.label: Events and relations
fields.what: What happened, who took part, and how things connect. Related tags (Gaza / Gaza Strip / Palestinians) merge by similarity; identity needs entity linking.

layers.name: Understanding (downstream, does not block)
layers.asks: One consolidated explanation per capability, whoever said it, traced back to its sources. Where do new items agree, disagree or leave gaps?

fields.label: Consolidated knowledge
fields.what: How a capability works and best practice across the field, merged from many sources

fields.label: Agree, contradict, gap
fields.what: Check each new item against what we know and flag what is new or missing

fields.label: Claim, evidence, source
fields.what: Every statement traced to the source text it came from; the raw documents stay but are not the focus

next.headline: The first lap of the improvement loop is done; the second waits on five decisions.
next.body: The whole flow ran once on real data: evidence pool, live path, teacher labels, retrain, score, advisor. It made the chain faster and built labels and evidence; it left the topic score where it was (79.3% to 79.5% against human labels). Story type, size, change and traits are held back by the decider on purpose because their contracts are not confirmed. To train all six BitMob models the owner decides: the judge for story type, the definition of Condition for full articles, the seed for Areas, the list of Capabilities, and later the GPU retrain (7,190 of 10,000 new rows). Also open: topic threshold 700 or 500. Ledger L1157 to L1167. The Reading gates page (console 8100) shows the loop, the lap and these decisions. Lap two is under way on working defaults (research only): a 250-article test of the Condition definition found conditions in 10.4% of the gists. Decisions now five: story type judge (a-binary), Condition definition (A, triples as evidence), Areas and Capabilities (3 to 5 each, named by the owner), how many topic answers the decider gives (700 holds on a fresh slice), and the GPU retrain.
next.ask: judge for story type · Condition definition · Area seed · Capability list · topic threshold · GPU retrain

tried_groups.name: What worked
tried_groups.summary: Word counts and static vectors for everything, a frozen small encoder on routed items (now mdbr-leaf-mt, 22.6M), and regularisation tuned on a validation slice (topic +0.02, topic overfitting gap 0.103 to 0.042).

items.what: Word counts + logistic regression alone
items.result: Story type at teacher level (0.90), topic weak (0.54)
items.outcome: Kept for story type and as the always-on path

items.what: Static word vectors (potion-8M) + logistic regression
items.result: Topic 0.62; confidence is trustworthy (calibration error 0.04)
items.outcome: Kept (the base of every version)

items.result: Which-condition top-1 0.704 to 0.770, top-2 0.828 to 0.905
items.outcome: Adopted, routed items only (v3)

tried_groups.name: Swapping the trunk (Granite small R2)
tried_groups.summary: Ties with bge-small on every Pulse field (short items). On whole articles a bigger window beats truncating at 512, but chunking bge-small beats one long Granite pass and costs far less CPU. Plan for long articles: bge-small chunks feeding tag-level joins.

items.what: ibm-granite/granite-embedding-small-english-r2 as the shared encoder (47.7M, Apache-2.0, 8k, ModernBERT), same heads and items
items.result: Topic top-2 0.881 vs 0.877, which-condition 0.875 vs 0.863, all inside the noise; encoder alone 23 ms; engine p95 44.5 ms vs 36.2; memory 837 MB vs 732

items.result: Neighbour topic agreement 0.634 vs 0.648; cluster agreement (NMI) 0.383 vs 0.408; 8,192 tokens 22 s vs about 3.9 s chunked
items.outcome: Granite not ahead; one test left (token-level tagging head, needs the Area tag labels)

items.what: Whole-article test: can a passage from the late part find its article? (1,500 long articles, median 1,078 tokens)
items.result: bge truncated 0.50; Granite whole article 0.64; bge chunked mean 0.77; bge best chunk 0.87 (recall@1, late passages)
items.outcome: Owner's logic holds (bigger window beats truncation); chunking a small model wins

tried_groups.name: Bigger or tuned neural models
tried_groups.summary: Fine-tuning, int8 and distilling the encoder were not better, or not fast enough.

items.what: Fine-tuning the encoder
items.result: First try much worse (topic top-2 0.726); corrected try +0.014 on topic but worse on which-condition
items.outcome: Rejected: frozen features beat it

items.what: int8 encoder to make it fast enough
items.result: Topic top-2 drops 0.019 against a 0.01 limit
items.outcome: Rejected; cascade instead

items.result: Keeps none of the encoder's lift (topic top-2 0.813 vs 0.832)
items.outcome: Rejected

tried_groups.name: Outside language models (d1, LFM3)
tried_groups.summary: d1 is a strong second opinion (topic 0.926 when combined) but needs the GPU and its licence does not fit. LFM3 is unusable.

items.what: d1-2B decision model, zero-shot, on the GPU
items.result: Alone: topic top-2 0.852. Fused with our student: topic top-2 0.926, condition top-1 0.834
items.outcome: Pipeline test only: GPU, and a licence the owner called not commercially viable

items.what: LFM3-1.7B as a JSON reader
items.result: Only 28% valid JSON; as a yes/no scorer AUC 0.54 to 0.61
items.outcome: Rejected

tried_groups.summary: Training our student on d1's soft labels gave no gain.

items.what: Training the student on d1's soft labels
items.result: Topic top-2 -0.008, story -0.006, which-condition +0.009 to +0.02
items.outcome: No gain; d1 stays a live second opinion

tried_groups.name: Free-form tags (pilot: 100 articles, 100 headline items)
tried_groups.summary: CPU proposes, Clef verifies: about 3 tags per headline item, 5.4 per full article; wording agreement about 0.5; 77% of tags occur once. Capabilities are 7% of general-news tags and 23% of tech-news tags, and almost never recur across articles: news can propose capability candidates but cannot supply the capability layer. Design: a hybrid.

items.what: Tag pilot with spaCy proposer and local Clef verifier (5 narrow yes/no questions per candidate)
items.result: 41% of 2,762 candidates accepted; kappa 0.49 to 0.53; merge at cosine 0.80 cuts distinct tags by 33% but merges related, not only identical, tags; 56% of full-article tags are absent from the short version
items.outcome: Hybrid design; capability layer needs tech sources; a token-level tag head is the serving route (the proposer takes 0.7 s per item)

changes.title: Four labellers agree on conditions; the sharper rule A did not help
changes.text: Four independent Sonnet labellers did the conditions field for the same 100 gists. Under the registered prompt two of them agree with kappa 0.80 (range 0.666 to 0.918) and match kind and direction on every item both called. Under a sharper rule A the pair reaches 0.72. Both of my predictions missed, and I had said the teacher's condition call was unstable by labeller; it is not (ledger correction L1182). The batch differences (10.4%, 4.0%, 5.7%) come from the items and from sampling. Same model family on both sides: agreement, not outside truth. Rule A is dropped. Ledger L1181, L1182.

changes.title: Fresh-slice check and a CPU condition-presence head
changes.text: Fresh MN-DS slice scored once (1,545 articles, human labels): all articles 78.5%; threshold 700 answers 67.5% at 82.7%, 500 answers 92.9% at 79.5%, just under the 0.80 line, so the setting stays at 700 (an advisor suggestion to set 500 was not followed; ledger L1176). A condition-presence sparse head on CPU scores F1 0.64 against Sonnet on the sealed set (always saying yes: 0.20). The agreement claims stand against their base rates (story type 91.5% against always-fact 84.5%). Two more teacher batches found conditions in 4.9% of 494 gists against 10.4% in the first 250; the stability test below shows that difference does not come from the labeller. Ledger L1175 to L1178.

changes.title: Condition test on a working definition: the change lexicon is a proposer, not an answer
changes.text: A teacher batch of 250 gists, picked from the rebalanced pool, gave 26 with a condition (10.4%), against 1.6% in the first 1,000. The change lexicon proposed a condition for 239 of the 250 and the teacher confirmed 23 (precision 9.6%); its proposals cover 88.5% of the teacher's conditions. Good for choosing articles to label, unfit as an answer. The rise from 1.6% is not credited to the proposals alone: the topic mix changed too. Working definition (a thing, a kind and a direction already changed), not a confirmed contract. Ledger L1171, L1172.

changes.title: Sparse heads can answer first and skip the encoder (behind a switch, off by default)
changes.text: A sparse topic head and a sparse story-type head, trained on Sonnet labels only, answer when both are confident and the encoder is skipped. Topic against human labels: chain 79.8% with the sparse head answering half, against 79.9% for v6b alone. On 200 full articles the encoder is skipped for 22.0% and the median time falls from 75.0 to 60.5 ms with the same answers. Whole chain on 1,600 human-labelled articles: 79.3% off, 79.5% on. Weak on forecast and opinion, so v6b still carries those. Ledger L1119, L1134, L1137, L1147.

changes.title: The toolchain read 20,000 articles in 243 seconds
changes.text: Every article through the scan, span rules, fact extractors, name finder, place linker, factuality tagger and change lexicon, each item stored with its strength: 92.0% of articles have at least one amount or date that passed all four checks (strength proved); everything else is rule. Ledger L1144, L1145.

changes.title: Triples find events the fact extractors miss; negation from triples helps the factuality tagger
changes.text: Against 6,029 human-marked events the open-extraction triples find the event word in 87.9%, the extractors' who-did-what in 72.6%; keep both. Taking certain, negated or possible from the triples lifts the factuality tagger's balanced accuracy from 0.4716 to 0.5428 and negated events caught from 17 to 46 of 151. Ledger L1129, L1143.

changes.title: Boilerplate strip and a retrain with 1,000 teacher labels moved nothing
changes.text: Boilerplate strip changed 0 of 36,092 training texts (labelled texts have no line breaks) and left the topic score at 75.5%. The sparse heads refit with 1,000 weak gist labels: topic 75.4% against 75.5%; the new rows are 2.7% of the training set. The teacher reading only the gist agrees with its full-article label on 83.0% of topics and 94.0% of story types (100 articles, same teacher). Ledger L1133, L1156, L1157.

changes.title: Topic confidence threshold: a coverage choice, not a tuning win
changes.text: At threshold 700 the decider answers topic on 60.6% of articles at 83.1% right against human labels; the withheld 39.4% are still 73.5% right. At 500 it answers 89.7% at 81.3%. A split-half test chose 300 on one half and 500 on the other, so confidence separates right from wrong only weakly. Not applied; the owner chooses. Ledger L1149, L1162.

changes.title: Wiring the sparse heads was first 21 times slower
changes.text: One scikit-learn probability call on a single sparse row took 1.5 s; the same sums as one matrix product take 0.08 ms and match to 6e-07. Fixed and rerun. Ledger L1136, L1137.

changes.title: Amounts, dates, names and triples now have a validator
changes.text: Stated facts are checked against the text itself, not against labellers: amounts pass all four checks 97.5%, dates 90.9%, names 40.7% (most names are modifiers and stay unbound), complete subject-verb-object triples 49.7% of fragments. Two flaws found and fixed while measuring (the scanner hid dates inside names; a date's day number counted as an amount). Ledger L958, L959.

changes.title: Direction and size taken off the condition chain
changes.text: They sat as 'blocked until condition is ready' for days. Now each is scored on its own: direction learned from the story text reaches 84.2% over every story against 78.4% for always up (falls 77% found, 80% needed); size is read as the stated amount, found in 27% of condition stories and 98% a real quantity. Ledger L951 to L954, L932.

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

fitness.name: Field checks v2
fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?
measures.m: Krippendorff's alpha: agreement beyond chance (1 = perfect, 0 = no better than guessing)

measures.q: Does agreement hold when a model from a different maker (Qwen3-14B) votes with Sonnet and Haiku?
measures.m: alpha over Sonnet, Haiku (one maker) and Qwen on the 395 items
measures.bar: same bands as the agreement score; a flag only, it does not change the verdict

measures.q: Does each answer agree, the rare ones too?
Do Sonnet and Haiku agree, not just each with itself? Same maker, so this is not an independent check.
How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?
measures.bar: ours: 10% or less ok · over 20% fail

measures.q: Does one model repeat itself?
measures.cite: none found (stability is not correctness: arXiv 2609.15194)

fit_tests.q: Would careful readers give the same answer?
fit_tests.m: the Agreement score above
fit_tests.bar: same bands as agreement score

fit_tests.q: Does every answer have enough cases to learn and to score?
fit_tests.m: cases per answer on the 395 four-vote items (the full labelled pool is larger, with one voter)
fit_tests.bar: ours: 30+ per answer; under that the answer needs targeted data
fit_tests.cite: LESSONS #8 (our notes); Graham & Bull 1998 uses 200+ for intervals

fit_tests.q: Is there trusted outside labelled data?
fit_tests.m: named outside dataset for the field
fit_tests.bar: none = agreement only: the field can never be called correct
fit_tests.src: our design; datasets named in playbook 01

fit_tests.m: agreement between headline-only and full-article labels

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).

Sonnet and Haiku come from one maker and share habits, so they count as one source; Qwen3-14B is the first independent maker (measured: same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on every field, L572).
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.

Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

rows.line: Sealed set: 91.5% agreement with Sonnet (90.0% to 92.8%), always saying 'fact' gets 84.5%. No outside anchor yet (T30). Held back by the decider: the contract is not confirmed and CheckThat scores fact versus opinion, not our four types (field table).

Two guesses: 92.2% agreement with Sonnet on the sealed set (best constant pair 38.2%); 79.9% against human labels (MN-DS, fresh articles), right at the 80% line. Whole chain on the human labels: 79.3% with the sparse heads off, 79.5% on; the decider answers 60.6% of articles (threshold 700).
Parked at the field gate after two definition rounds. v6b-student finds 29.3% of real cases and its end-to-end 86.3% is below simply saying no (89.1%). No gross false-yes errors in the outside check.
Only meaningful on articles that have a condition. 79.2%, 3 points short.
Learned from the story on its own: right 84.2% over 3,871 stories against 78.4% for always up; finds 77% of real falls (80% needed). Agreement with Sonnet, not outside truth (L954).

Read as the stated amount and checked against the text: 97.5% of 5,323 amounts pass all four checks (in the text, value reads back, bound to a noun or verb, one sentence). Spot check: 87% are the condition's own. Replaces small / notable / large. Stated is not true (L959). Held back by the decider until its contract is confirmed.

Counted per trait, not one pass or fail: 2 of 51 traits are GO (deaths or injuries; a household price went up, revised wording). engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread. From 2026-11-05 the same reader also serves per-condition heads for four kinds (air pollution, biodiversity loss, civil unrest, cyber insecurity) and a direction head for biodiversity loss, on the same embedding, 16.6 ms median over HTTP (service pulse_reader, route /v1/pulse; nothing calls it yet). Since 2026-11-08 an optional pair of sparse heads (topic and story type) can answer first and skip the encoder when both are confident; off by default (ledger L1137).
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built. Exception (owner, 2026-11-05): direction and size are read from the story text and scored on their own; they do not wait on condition.

next.headline: The first lap of the improvement loop is done; the second waits on five decisions.
next.body: The whole flow ran once on real data: evidence pool, live path, teacher labels, retrain, score, advisor. It made the chain faster and built labels and evidence; it left the topic score where it was (79.3% to 79.5% against human labels). Story type, size, change and traits are held back by the decider on purpose because their contracts are not confirmed. To train all six BitMob models the owner decides: the judge for story type, the definition of Condition for full articles, the seed for Areas, the list of Capabilities, and later the GPU retrain (7,190 of 10,000 new rows). Also open: topic threshold 700 or 500. Ledger L1157 to L1167. The Reading gates page (console 8100) shows the loop, the lap and these decisions. Lap two is under way on working defaults (research only): a 250-article test of the Condition definition found conditions in 10.4% of the gists. Decisions now five: story type judge (a-binary), Condition definition (A, triples as evidence), Areas and Capabilities (3 to 5 each, named by the owner), how many topic answers the decider gives (working decision 600, which holds on two fresh slices; say 700 to keep the old setting), and the GPU retrain. The loop's work is now recorded as tasks T43 to T47 (Map and Work tabs).

changes.title: Topic setting 600 holds on two fresh slices
changes.text: A second fresh MN-DS slice (1,352 articles, scored once, human labels): 600 answers 82.5% of articles at 80.8%; 700 answers 69.5% at 82.2%; 500 answers 91.9% at 79.5%, just under the 0.80 line (it was also under it on the first slice). Every prediction held. Working decision: 600; 700 stays the prototype default until the reader is served; the owner can veto. The slice has an uneven category mix. Ledger L1181, L1209.

changes.title: Four labellers agree on conditions; the sharper rule A did not help
changes.text: Four independent Sonnet labellers did the conditions field for the same 100 gists. Under the registered prompt two of them agree with kappa 0.80 (range 0.666 to 0.918) and match kind and direction on every item both called. Under a sharper rule A the pair reaches 0.72. Both of my predictions missed, and I had said the teacher's condition call was unstable by labeller; it is not (ledger correction L1182). The batch differences (10.4%, 4.0%, 5.7%) come from the items and from sampling. Same model family on both sides: agreement, not outside truth. Rule A is dropped. Ledger L1181, L1182.

changes.title: Fresh-slice check and a CPU condition-presence head
changes.text: Fresh MN-DS slice scored once (1,545 articles, human labels): all articles 78.5%; threshold 700 answers 67.5% at 82.7%, 500 answers 92.9% at 79.5%, just under the 0.80 line, so the setting stays at 700 (an advisor suggestion to set 500 was not followed; ledger L1176). A condition-presence sparse head on CPU scores F1 0.64 against Sonnet on the sealed set (always saying yes: 0.20). The agreement claims stand against their base rates (story type 91.5% against always-fact 84.5%). Two more teacher batches found conditions in 4.9% of 494 gists against 10.4% in the first 250; the stability test below shows that difference does not come from the labeller. Ledger L1175 to L1178.

changes.title: Condition test on a working definition: the change lexicon is a proposer, not an answer
changes.text: A teacher batch of 250 gists, picked from the rebalanced pool, gave 26 with a condition (10.4%), against 1.6% in the first 1,000. The change lexicon proposed a condition for 239 of the 250 and the teacher confirmed 23 (precision 9.6%); its proposals cover 88.5% of the teacher's conditions. Good for choosing articles to label, unfit as an answer. The rise from 1.6% is not credited to the proposals alone: the topic mix changed too. Working definition (a thing, a kind and a direction already changed), not a confirmed contract. Ledger L1171, L1172.

changes.title: Sparse heads can answer first and skip the encoder (behind a switch, off by default)
changes.text: A sparse topic head and a sparse story-type head, trained on Sonnet labels only, answer when both are confident and the encoder is skipped. Topic against human labels: chain 79.8% with the sparse head answering half, against 79.9% for v6b alone. On 200 full articles the encoder is skipped for 22.0% and the median time falls from 75.0 to 60.5 ms with the same answers. Whole chain on 1,600 human-labelled articles: 79.3% off, 79.5% on. Weak on forecast and opinion, so v6b still carries those. Ledger L1119, L1134, L1137, L1147.

changes.title: The toolchain read 20,000 articles in 243 seconds
changes.text: Every article through the scan, span rules, fact extractors, name finder, place linker, factuality tagger and change lexicon, each item stored with its strength: 92.0% of articles have at least one amount or date that passed all four checks (strength proved); everything else is rule. Ledger L1144, L1145.

changes.title: Triples find events the fact extractors miss; negation from triples helps the factuality tagger
changes.text: Against 6,029 human-marked events the open-extraction triples find the event word in 87.9%, the extractors' who-did-what in 72.6%; keep both. Taking certain, negated or possible from the triples lifts the factuality tagger's balanced accuracy from 0.4716 to 0.5428 and negated events caught from 17 to 46 of 151. Ledger L1129, L1143.

changes.title: Boilerplate strip and a retrain with 1,000 teacher labels moved nothing
changes.text: Boilerplate strip changed 0 of 36,092 training texts (labelled texts have no line breaks) and left the topic score at 75.5%. The sparse heads refit with 1,000 weak gist labels: topic 75.4% against 75.5%; the new rows are 2.7% of the training set. The teacher reading only the gist agrees with its full-article label on 83.0% of topics and 94.0% of story types (100 articles, same teacher). Ledger L1133, L1156, L1157.

changes.title: Topic confidence threshold: a coverage choice, not a tuning win
changes.text: At threshold 700 the decider answers topic on 60.6% of articles at 83.1% right against human labels; the withheld 39.4% are still 73.5% right. At 500 it answers 89.7% at 81.3%. A split-half test chose 300 on one half and 500 on the other, so confidence separates right from wrong only weakly. Not applied; the owner chooses. Ledger L1149, L1162.

changes.title: Wiring the sparse heads was first 21 times slower
changes.text: One scikit-learn probability call on a single sparse row took 1.5 s; the same sums as one matrix product take 0.08 ms and match to 6e-07. Fixed and rerun. Ledger L1136, L1137.

changes.title: Amounts, dates, names and triples now have a validator
changes.text: Stated facts are checked against the text itself, not against labellers: amounts pass all four checks 97.5%, dates 90.9%, names 40.7% (most names are modifiers and stay unbound), complete subject-verb-object triples 49.7% of fragments. Two flaws found and fixed while measuring (the scanner hid dates inside names; a date's day number counted as an amount). Ledger L958, L959.

changes.title: Direction and size taken off the condition chain
changes.text: They sat as 'blocked until condition is ready' for days. Now each is scored on its own: direction learned from the story text reaches 84.2% over every story against 78.4% for always up (falls 77% found, 80% needed); size is read as the stated amount, found in 27% of condition stories and 98% a real quantity. Ledger L951 to L954, L932.

changes.title: Adopted v6b-student after one sealed-set scoring
changes.text: Sealed set scored once (1,499 items, 2.19 USD hosted): story 91.5%, topic two guesses 92.2%, real conditions found 29.3%, all better than v5-leaf (87.1%, 90.1%, 22.0%). Ledger L771.

changes.title: Challenger v6b-student: ADOPTED 2026-11-04 (was waiting for your yes)
changes.text: A 22M student (same size as today's encoder) taught by a 4B reader on the GPU, trained on about 16,000 Sonnet labels; one CPU pass per item, no GPU at serving. On 1,593 fresh items it never trained or tuned on: story type 88.8% to 91.8% (+3.0, interval 1.5 to 4.5), topic one guess 78.6% to 81.9% (+3.3), real conditions found 17.5% to 32.5% (+15 points, 9 to 21), condition-direction-size all right 15.1% to 25.9% (+10.8), which condition 79.2% to 82.7% (+3.6, 1,176 cases). Speed 15 ms typical, 17 ms at 95% (v5-leaf: 4.4 ms typical, 23 ms at 95% with rare multi-second stalls), 595 MB. Agreement with Sonnet, not accuracy. Earlier 6,000-label version: v6-student.

changes.title: Condition tiers, read from a curve
changes.text: On 1,593 fresh items (166 real conditions), v6b-student finds more real conditions than v5-leaf at every level of 'how sure the yes is': at 95% right 31% vs 13%, at 90% right 36% vs 22%, at 83% right 39% vs 28%, at 75% right 55% vs 33%, at 60% right 71% vs 58%. A confident tier (about 90% right) would flag about 41 items per 1,000 and find about 36% of real conditions; a possible tier (about 60% right) about 123 per 1,000 and find about 71%. Which tier the engine speaks at is your decision.

changes.title: Topic
changes.text: One guess 0.698 to 0.747 and two guesses 0.831 to 0.896 from v1 to v5, on 1,997 natural unseen items (agreement with Sonnet).

changes.title: Speed and memory
changes.text: 95% of reads under 23 ms (v3.2: 36 ms) and 643 MB (v3.2: 734 MB) after the switch to the leaf encoder.

changes.title: Honest measuring
changes.text: Every figure now comes from 1,997 natural, never-seen items. Older figures (story 0.911, real conditions found 10%) came from a condition-enriched test set and are replaced: story 0.875, found 20%.

changes.title: Story type, condition answering
changes.text: Flat since v1 (story 0.875; condition answers 0.966 on the 80% it answers; real conditions found 19.9%).

changes.title: Finding real conditions: 5 levers tried
changes.text: Lowering the cut, adding the encoder to the presence gate, training the which-condition head on Sonnet, reweighting the blend, and 38 per-condition detectors. None lifts the share found at 83% right above a third (33%).

changes.title: Story and topic trained on Sonnet labels
changes.text: The engine learns from 36,070 Haiku labels; Haiku and Sonnet agree on story type only 93% of the time. Test running, pass bar +0.02.

changes.title: Traits (51 questions)
changes.text: Wording tested on 150 items: 50 of 51 pass the pilot rule; Sonnet agrees with itself on 87% of its active answers. Student heads training on 2,500 Sonnet-graded items.

changes.title: Real conditions: counts
changes.text: The which / direction / size rows above rest on only 44 and 38 found items (the easy slice). New rows use all 1,176 real conditions we hold: which condition 79.2% (77 to 81), direction 88.2%, size 93.6%, all three right 64.9%.

changes.title: Next for the challenger
changes.text: Rerun with 16,000 Sonnet labels (10,000 more are being labelled), a second training sweep, and the sealed test once at the end.

changes.title: Traits: first results
changes.text: Sonnet graded 2,650 items on 51 questions (agrees with itself 87% on active answers). On the CPU reader, 24 of 51 questions work as present/absent flags; a 4B reader adds only a little (30 of 51). Next: build the flags into the engine, or label more graded examples.

fitness.name: Field checks v2
fitness.rule: Consensus verdict uses ONLY the sourced agreement score bands (Krippendorff 2004, p.241): 0.80 or more clear, 0.667 to 0.80 tentative, under 0.667 reject. Our own measures are flags and never decide.

measures.q: Do labellers agree beyond chance?
measures.m: Krippendorff's alpha: agreement beyond chance (1 = perfect, 0 = no better than guessing)

measures.q: Does agreement hold when a model from a different maker (Qwen3-14B) votes with Sonnet and Haiku?
measures.m: alpha over Sonnet, Haiku (one maker) and Qwen on the 395 items
measures.bar: same bands as the agreement score; a flag only, it does not change the verdict

measures.q: Does each answer agree, the rare ones too?
Do Sonnet and Haiku agree, not just each with itself? Same maker, so this is not an independent check.
How many items have no 3-of-4 majority?
measures.bar: ours: 10% or less ok · over 20% fail

measures.q: Does one model repeat itself?
measures.cite: none found (stability is not correctness: arXiv 2609.15194)

fit_tests.q: Would careful readers give the same answer?
fit_tests.m: the Agreement score above
fit_tests.bar: same bands as agreement score

fit_tests.q: Does every answer have enough cases to learn and to score?
fit_tests.m: cases per answer on the 395 four-vote items (the full labelled pool is larger, with one voter)
fit_tests.bar: ours: 30+ per answer; under that the answer needs targeted data
fit_tests.cite: LESSONS #8 (our notes); Graham & Bull 1998 uses 200+ for intervals

fit_tests.q: Is there trusted outside labelled data?
fit_tests.m: named outside dataset for the field
fit_tests.bar: none = agreement only: the field can never be called correct
fit_tests.src: our design; datasets named in playbook 01

fit_tests.q: Does the headline plus description carry the evidence?
fit_tests.m: agreement between headline-only and full-article labels
fit_tests.bar: not measured yet

assumptions: The 395-item sample represents the news pool beyond its stratification (about half real conditions).

Sonnet and Haiku come from one maker and share habits, so they count as one source; Qwen3-14B is the first independent maker (measured: same-maker agreement is higher than cross-maker on every field, L572).
Krippendorff's bands, set for human coders, also suit LLM voters.
The Lean models cover two coders and two answers; the pipeline uses 4 voters and up to 40 answers.
Catching planted bugs predicts catching real ones; the references, Lean models and fixtures were all written by us, so a shared misreading would survive every method.
MM3's quick 9-question form says nothing about its thorough form.
Sources were read as search summaries; none of the papers was opened.
notes: Traits (51 questions) were scored under the old rule and are not shown until rescored.
Fit and Consensus were one column called 'Fit' before 2026-11-02. Consensus is how well the labels hold up; Fit is whether the field is worth classifying at all.
Source tags: 'sourced' = a published criterion; 'ours' = our own bar or design, not validated.
Story type's κ is 0.58 but its skew-resistant AC1 is 0.92; condition present's κ 0.37 and AC1 0.38 match, so its disagreement is real, not skew (ledger L515).
fitness.clef: Clef agrees with Sonnet 63% and with Haiku 63% on presence (a different question wording); on the 162 split items it matches majority 57%, so it cannot arbitrate them.

notes: Only items dated after the 2026-10-25 training cutoff are scored. The first run on all 395 items was contaminated (story type 98%) and was discarded.
86 items means wide ranges (story type v5-leaf 85 to 97%). This shows direction, not a verdict.
Set is 69% real conditions, so Condition present: right is judged against always-yes.
Direction and size have under 12 scorable items and are not scored.

plain.blocker: Story type and topic are ready; the reader that serves them is v6b-student (15 ms, one CPU thread). Condition is parked: the CPU reader finds about 3 in 10 real cases. Direction and size no longer wait behind it: direction is learned from the story at 84.2% (guessing up: 78.4%), size is read as the stated amount (found in 27% of condition stories, 98% a real quantity).

rows.line: Sealed set: 91.5% agreement with Sonnet (90.0% to 92.8%), always saying 'fact' gets 84.5%. No outside anchor yet (T30). Held back by the decider: the contract is not confirmed and CheckThat scores fact versus opinion, not our four types (field table).

Two guesses: 92.2% agreement with Sonnet on the sealed set (best constant pair 38.2%); 79.9% against human labels (MN-DS, fresh articles), right at the 80% line. Whole chain on the human labels: 79.3% with the sparse heads off, 79.5% on; the decider answers 60.6% of articles (threshold 700).
Parked at the field gate after two definition rounds. v6b-student finds 29.3% of real cases and its end-to-end 86.3% is below simply saying no (89.1%). No gross false-yes errors in the outside check.
Only meaningful on articles that have a condition. 79.2%, 3 points short.
Learned from the story on its own: right 84.2% over 3,871 stories against 78.4% for always up; finds 77% of real falls (80% needed). Agreement with Sonnet, not outside truth (L954).

Read as the stated amount and checked against the text: 97.5% of 5,323 amounts pass all four checks (in the text, value reads back, bound to a noun or verb, one sentence). Spot check: 87% are the condition's own. Replaces small / notable / large. Stated is not true (L959). Held back by the decider until its contract is confirmed.

Counted per trait, not one pass or fail: 2 of 51 traits are GO (deaths or injuries; a household price went up, revised wording). Two others failed the gate (a threat to the natural environment, a single city or smaller area). 45 need a wording revision, 2 need more positive examples. The row is Ready when you name the traits the product needs and all of them are GO.

engine.name: BitMob Expert 1
engine.how: Every item is read by fast linear models on word counts and static word vectors. About a third of items, the ones a cheap first pass flags, also go through a small encoder: MongoDB's mdbr-leaf-mt (22.6M parameters, 6 layers, 512 tokens). Long articles are cut into chunks. From 2026-11-04 the reader is v6b-student: the same sparse parts plus a fine-tuned copy of that encoder (22.6M parameters, distilled from 16,000 Sonnet labels) that reads story type, topic, condition presence and which condition in one pass; 15 ms typical on one CPU thread. From 2026-11-05 the same reader also serves per-condition heads for four kinds (air pollution, biodiversity loss, civil unrest, cyber insecurity) and a direction head for biodiversity loss, on the same embedding, 16.6 ms median over HTTP (service pulse_reader, route /v1/pulse; nothing calls it yet). Since 2026-11-08 an optional pair of sparse heads (topic and story type) can answer first and skip the encoder when both are confident; off by default (ledger L1137).
engine.why: Linear models alone already match Sonnet on story type. The encoder adds the most on which-condition and topic. Chosen from the full field of 215 scored models: in our size class it ties on every Pulse field, is about 40% faster than bge-small (95% of reads under 23 ms), uses 80 MB less memory, and joins related articles better. Adopted after one scoring on the sealed 1,499 items (ledger L771): better than v5-leaf on story type, topic and real conditions found; condition is still Not ready.
engine.teacher: claude-sonnet-5-5 (frozen guideline). Agreement with Sonnet, never accuracy: no human gold.
engine.bar_note: Owner's working figure: agreement of 80% or more on the items it answers.
engine.rule: Ready needs all four: (1) counted over every item, a skipped item is a miss, and the low end of the 95% range is 80% or more; (2) the low end beats always guessing the most common answer; (3) if the field finds something rare, it finds 80% or more of the real cases; (4) 30+ items, and a step that depends on an earlier one waits until that one is Ready. Partial = 80% or more only on the items it answers (it answers at least half). Not yet = anything else. Later phase = not built. Exception (owner, 2026-11-05): direction and size are read from the story text and scored on their own; they do not wait on condition.
